## Claude Code permission model for AGI TUI

<a id="claude-permissions"></a>

Ordered allow/ask/deny.

**Key findings**

- Three behaviors allow/ask/deny; passthrough is internal and becomes ask
- Fixed ordered pipeline not a flat list: deny>ask>allow, bypass-immune ask/safetyCheck (permissions.ts:1071-1319)
- Modes default/acceptEdits/plan/bypassPermissions/dontAsk + experimental auto; Shift+Tab cycles; acceptEdits allowlist mkdir/touch/rm/rmdir/mv/cp/sed
- Matchers: prefix colon-star word-boundary, wildcard git-star trailing-optional, gitignore paths, WebFetch domain
- Rules merge Managed>CLI>Local>Project>User; scalars override; policy/flag/command read-only
- AlwaysAllow writes a durable rule (addRules) to a scope; AllowSession is in-memory session
- safetyCheck is a separate mode-independent bypass-immune gate

**Recommendations for AGI**

- Add a rule-matching engine (allow/ask/deny by source) implementing the exact ordered pipeline before the prompt
- Make safety/approval.rs a bypass-immune safetyCheck layer gating even in BypassPermissions/DontAsk
- Persist AlwaysAllow as a scoped settings.json rule (Project/Local/User); AllowSession stays in-memory
- Adopt Claude rule grammar/matchers for .claude-style portability
- Settings hierarchy Managed>CLI>Local>Project>User: merge rules, override scalars, read-only managed deny
- Shift+Tab mode cycle + active-mode footer; honor defaultMode and --permission-mode
- Attach a decisionReason to every outcome and show it in the overlay (never-silent)

**Conflicts (docs vs local reference)**

- Docs moved: claude-code/iam now auth-only; permissions schema on code.claude.com/docs/en/settings; IAM-page permission refs are stale
- defaultMode: docs show six incl auto; ref lists five and gates auto behind TRANSCRIPT_CLASSIFIER; both agree auto is conditional
- CLI flags: docs don't enumerate allowedTools/disallowedTools but they are real flags; source code wins

## Claude Code slash commands (built-in + custom), argument hints, and the command-popup UX — conventions for AGI's Rust/Ratatui CLI command palette

<a id="claude-slash"></a>

Claude Code recognizes slash commands only at the start of a message; everything after the command name is passed as a single argument string. There are ~80 built-in commands (e.g. /help, /clear, /compact, /init, /model, /mcp, /agents, /skills, /resume, /rewind, /context, /usage, /review), some of which are prompt-based "bundled skills" badged differently from fixed-logic built-ins. The big architectural shift in current docs: custom commands have been MERGED into skills — `.claude/commands/deploy.md` (filename = command) and `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` (directory = command) both produce `/deploy` and share the same frontmatter; if both exist the skill wins. Commands resolve across managed > user (`~/.claude`) > project (`.claude/` walked up to git root) scopes, with MCP-provided prompts surfaced as `/mcp__<server>__<prompt>` and plugin commands namespaced `plugin:name`. The popup is a fuzzy-filtered (Fuse.js, threshold 0.3) typeahead that on empty `/` shows recently-used skills first, then built-ins, then user/project/policy commands alphabetically; it renders `/<name>` left and a gray description right, suppresses itself once an argument is typed, supports inline ghost-text completion, and shows a per-field `argument-hint` plus a progressive remaining-args hint. Argument substitution supports `$ARGUMENTS`, `$ARGUMENTS[N]`/`$N`, named `$foo` (from `arguments:` frontmatter), plus `!`backtick``dynamic shell injection and`@file` references.

**Key findings**

- Two-column popup layout: left = `/<name>` (with `(alias)` only when the user typed the alias), right = description, wrapped to ~2 lines with hanging indent. Bordered by horizontal divider rules above and below the input line. This is the layout AGI's Ratatui palette should mirror (see palette .txt screenshots).
- Empty-`/` ordering is deliberate and NOT alphabetical overall: recently-used skills (top 5 by usage score) -> built-in commands -> user commands -> project commands -> policy commands -> other; each sub-group sorted alphabetically. Built-ins are deliberately surfaced high so they stay visible when many skills are installed.
- Filtering is fuzzy (Fuse.js, threshold 0.3) over name(weight 3)/name-parts(2)/aliases(2)/description(0.5), then RE-SORTED by a hand-written comparator: exact-name > exact-alias > prefix-name (shorter wins) > prefix-alias > fuzzy-score, with usage frequency as the final tiebreaker. A pure fuzzy score alone is not enough — exact/prefix promotion matters for feel.
- argument-hint is a first-class affordance: a static gray hint (e.g. `[issue-number]` or `[filename] [format]`) from frontmatter shown after the command, PLUS a dynamic progressive hint that shows only the REMAINING unfilled named args as the user types. The popup hides entirely once a real argument is present (`hasCommandArgs`).
- Custom commands are now skills: a markdown file in `.claude/commands/<name>.md` (command name = filename) and a `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (command name = directory) are equivalent; skill wins on name clash. Scopes resolve managed > user(`~/.claude`) > project(`.claude/` walked up to git root). Plugin commands are namespaced `plugin:name`; MCP prompts appear as `/mcp__<server>__<prompt>`.
- Rich frontmatter contract worth emulating: description, argument-hint, arguments (named positional), allowed-tools/disallowed-tools, model, effort, disable-model-invocation (user-only), user-invocable:false (model-only/hidden from menu), context:fork + agent (run as subagent), paths (only surface after matching files touched). Visibility states beyond on/off: name-only, user-invocable-only.
- Argument substitution + dynamic context are part of the command body, not just args: `$ARGUMENTS`/`$ARGUMENTS[N]`/`$N`/named `$foo`, with `!`cmd``shell injection (output inlined BEFORE the model sees it; only at line-start or after whitespace) and`@file`references. Shell-quote parsing means`"multi word"` becomes one positional arg.
- Commands are recognized only at the START of a message (mid-input `/` triggers ghost-text completion but not execution); some commands are `immediate` (bypass the queue), and `isSensitive` commands redact their args from history. Workflow-backed commands get a distinct `workflow` tag/badge in the list.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- Build the palette as a two-pane row (left `/<name>` fixed-width column using a Ratatui token color, right dimmed description with wrapping) and render it inside a bordered block anchored just above the input — matching the divider-rule framing in the reference screenshots. Use design-token colors per the project's no-hardcoded-colors rule, not literal hex.
- Implement the empty-`/` ordering (recent -> builtin -> user -> project -> policy, alphabetical within group) and the exact>prefix>fuzzy re-sort with a usage-frequency tiebreaker. A bare fuzzy library result will feel wrong; the promotion logic is what makes the right command land at the top. Port the comparator from commandSuggestions.ts rather than reinventing it.
- Adopt the dual `argument-hint` model: a static gray hint after the command name AND a progressive 'remaining args' hint that shrinks as the user types each positional. Suppress the whole popup as soon as a non-empty argument follows the command (the `hasCommandArgs` rule).
- Standardize AGI's custom-command file contract on the merged commands+skills convention so AGI files are forward-compatible: support BOTH `.claude/commands/<name>.md` and `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, with skill-wins-on-clash and managed > user > project precedence; namespace plugin commands `plugin:name` and MCP prompts as `mcp__<server>__<prompt>`. Verify the exact AGI hook/skill event contract against `locks/cli-hooks-canonical-2026-05-23.md` before wiring.
- Support at least: description, argument-hint, arguments (named), allowed-tools, model, and disable-model-invocation in AGI's frontmatter parser — and the `$ARGUMENTS`/`$N`/`$name` substitution plus `!`cmd`` dynamic injection — since these are now the stable cross-tool Agent Skills standard. Treat `!`cmd`` injection as a security surface (gate behind a `disableSkillShellExecution`-equivalent policy for project/plugin sources, mirroring Claude Code).
- Add the `workflow`/`Skill` badge concept and per-command visibility states (on / name-only / user-invocable-only / off) so AGI can hide background-knowledge skills from the `/` menu while keeping them model-invocable — important for AGI's memory/personalization skills that shouldn't clutter the palette.
- Respect the 'command only at message start' rule and add inline ghost-text completion for the best prefix match (the getBestCommandMatch suffix pattern); also honor an `immediate` flag for commands that should bypass any input queue, and an `isSensitive` flag to redact args from transcript persistence.

**Conflicts (docs vs local reference)**

- Custom-command model: older training-data / earlier docs treat `.claude/commands/*.md` as the canonical custom-command mechanism, but current official docs (code.claude.com/docs/en/skills, accessed 2026-06-01) state custom commands have been MERGED INTO SKILLS and `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` is the recommended form, with the skill winning on name clash. Official docs win: they are current and the local reference's markdownConfigLoader.ts already lists both 'commands' and 'skills' in CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIRECTORIES, corroborating the merge. AGI should support both paths but treat skills as primary.
- Built-in command set drifts by version: the local reference palette screenshots are from v2.1.128 (e.g. show `/extra-usage`, `/skills`, `/sandbox`) while current docs list the renamed/added forms (`/usage-credits` replacing `/extra-usage`, `/reload-skills` added in 2.1.152, `/vim` removed in 2.1.92, `/pr-comments` removed in 2.1.91). The official commands reference wins for the CURRENT command inventory; the local screenshots win as ground truth for the PALETTE LAYOUT/RENDERING (they show real pixels, docs only describe behavior).
- Frontmatter field naming: local TS type uses camelCase internal fields (argumentHint, argNames, disableModelInvocation, userInvocable) while the on-disk/user-facing frontmatter uses kebab-case (argument-hint, arguments, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable). No real conflict — the loader maps kebab YAML keys to camelCase runtime fields; AGI's parser should accept the kebab-case keys users actually write (per official docs) and is free to use any internal representation.

## Claude Code Subagents and the Agent tool, formerly Task — AGI Rust and Ratatui Task and Subagent cell rendering

<a id="claude-subagents"></a>

Claude Code renders subagents spawned by the Agent tool (formerly Task) as grouped expandable transcript cells; details and AGI guidance are in the key findings and recommendations below.

**Key findings**

- Agent not Task since v2.1.63; subagent cells are grouped expandable blocks with header inverse-pill tree rows and a status sub-line and a deterministic Done summary; last 3 message throttle and short terminal condensed fallback; 8 color names; project and user agents discovery requiring name and description ordered and deduped by source.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- Add a SubagentCell mirroring AgentProgressLine on the existing TranscriptCell trait; port formatNumber and formatDuration and the Done summary; map 8 colors to Ratatui palette tokens as inverse pills; wire is_expandable and Ctrl-O to inline the nested transcript; label the tool Agent but accept Task as an alias; mirror agentDisplay and loadAgentsDir ordering and dedup for agents.

## Claude Code MCP integration (server config, tool namespacing, resources, prompts, elicitation/approval) — requirements for AGI's /mcp panel + MCP approval

<a id="claude-mcp"></a>

Claude Code connects to MCP servers over multiple transports (stdio, http/streamable-http, sse [deprecated], ws, plus internal sse-ide/ws-ide and sdk types) configured via `claude mcp add*` CLI commands and JSON config files. Servers carry a scope: docs surface three user-facing scopes (local→~/.claude.json per-project, project→.mcp.json in repo root, user→~/.claude.json global) with enterprise/managed and claude.ai layered on top, while the source enum (types.ts) actually defines seven (local, user, project, dynamic, enterprise, claudeai, managed); precedence is local > project > user > plugin > claude.ai, with the entire highest-precedence entry used (no field merge). MCP tools are exposed to the model under the namespaced name mcp**<server>**<tool> (built by buildMcpToolName via getMcpPrefix), where both server and tool segments pass normalizeNameForMCP (replaces any char outside [a-zA-Z0-9_-] with \_); permission rules and checks use this fully-qualified name so MCP tools can't collide with builtins. MCP prompts become slash commands /mcp**<server>**<prompt> (space-separated args), and resources are referenced with @server:protocol://resource/path @-mentions (backed by ListMcpResources/ReadMcpResource tools). Approval: project-scoped .mcp.json servers are gated by a 3-choice dialog (use this / use this+all future in project / continue without), persisted to local settings (enabledMcpjsonServers / disabledMcpjsonServers / enableAllProjectMcpServers), resettable via `claude mcp reset-project-choices`; individual MCP tool calls go through the normal tool-use permission flow (passthrough → addRules suggestion for the fully-qualified name); elicitation requests are handled mid-task in form or url mode with an Elicitation hook auto-response path.

**Key findings**

- Tool namespacing is the load-bearing contract: every MCP tool is exposed to the model as mcp**<server>**<tool>, built by buildMcpToolName->getMcpPrefix (mcpStringUtils.ts:39,50). Both segments pass normalizeNameForMCP (normalization.ts:17) replacing any char outside [a-zA-Z0-9_-] with _ to satisfy the API name pattern ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$. Inverse parse mcpInfoFromString (L19) splits on ** and has a documented ambiguity when a server name itself contains **.
- Permission identity must be the fully-qualified name. checkPermissions for an MCP tool returns behavior:'passthrough' plus an addRules suggestion whose rule targets mcp**server**tool (client.ts:1814-1831), and getToolNameForPermissionCheck (mcpStringUtils.ts:60) deliberately uses the qualified name so a deny rule on a builtin (e.g. 'Write') can't accidentally match an MCP tool sharing that display name. User-facing label is '${server} - ${title||tool} (MCP)'.
- Five distinct server connection states drive the panel UI (types.ts:180-226): connected (client+capabilities+tools/prompts/resources), failed (with error), needs-auth (OAuth/401-403), pending (connecting/reconnecting, carries reconnectAttempt/maxReconnectAttempts), disabled. Docs add /mcp shows a per-server tool count and flags servers that advertise the tools capability but expose zero tools, and that pending project servers show in `claude mcp list` as 'Pending approval'.
- Config is scope-layered with strict precedence (local > project > user > plugin > claude.ai); the entire highest-precedence entry wins with no cross-scope field merge. The three CLI-facing scopes map to files: local & user -> ~/.claude.json (local keyed per-project, user global), project -> .mcp.json in repo root (version-controlled, therefore the one gated by approval). Enterprise/managed (managed-mcp.json, allowedMcpServers/deniedMcpServers) and claude.ai connectors layer on top.
- Project-server approval is a 3-choice gate, not yes/no. MCPServerApprovalDialog offers 'Use this and all future MCP servers in this project' (yes_all -> enableAllProjectMcpServers:true), 'Use this MCP server' (yes -> append enabledMcpjsonServers), 'Continue without using this MCP server' (no -> append disabledMcpjsonServers). Choices persist to localSettings (.claude/settings.local.json) and reset via `claude mcp reset-project-choices`. This is separate from per-tool-call permission, which uses the normal tool-use flow.
- Prompts and resources are separate first-class surfaces. Prompts (prompts/list) become slash commands /mcp**server**prompt with space-separated positional args zipped onto the prompt's declared argument names (client.ts:2054-2095). Resources are @-mentioned as @server:protocol://resource/path, backed by two deferred read-only tools ListMcpResourcesTool and ReadMcpResourceTool (resources/read); binary blobs are persisted to disk and replaced with a path+message rather than inlined as base64.
- Elicitation is a mid-task interactive request with two modes: form (server-defined fields) and url (open browser, then confirm/skip in CLI, tracked by elicitationId + a completion notification). It is queued into app state and can be auto-answered or blocked by an Elicitation hook before any UI shows; only registered if the client declared elicitation capability (elicitationHandler.ts:68-212).
- MCP tools are deferred by default via Tool Search (only names load at session start; full schemas load on demand), with per-server alwaysLoad/anthropic/alwaysLoad and anthropic/searchHint/anthropic/maxResultSizeChars \_meta hints. Output is warned at 10k tokens and capped by MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS (default 25k). A panel should reflect always-loaded vs deferred status as context cost.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- /mcp panel: render servers grouped by scope and tag each with one of the five connection states from types.ts (connected/failed/needs-auth/pending/disabled) using a Ratatui palette token per state (no hardcoded colors). Show per-server tool count and an explicit 'advertises tools but exposes none' warning badge, mirror the pending/reconnecting state (attempt N/max), and surface a 'needs auth' action that triggers the OAuth flow.
- Implement namespacing exactly: store the unnormalized server+tool (the mcpInfo equivalent) but present/route the model-facing and permission-facing identity as mcp**<normalize(server)>**<normalize(tool)> via a single normalize fn equivalent to normalizeNameForMCP (regex [^a-zA-Z0-9_-] -> \_, segment cap 64). Reuse the fully-qualified name for all permission rule matching so MCP tools never collide with builtin names; preserve the documented \_\_-in-server-name caveat for the inverse parse.
- Approval model: implement the 3-option project-server dialog (this / this+all-future-in-project / continue-without), not a binary prompt, and persist choices to a local-settings store distinct from the server's scope storage. Keep 'local scope' (per-project server config) strictly separate from 'local settings' (approval state) in both data model and UI copy -- upstream docs call out this exact confusion. Provide a reset action equivalent to reset-project-choices.
- Per-tool-call permission: route MCP tool execution through AGI's existing approval broker (approval_broker.rs) keyed on the fully-qualified mcp**server**tool, defaulting to ask/passthrough, and offer an 'always allow this tool' rule written to local settings -- matching client.ts's addRules suggestion shape. Do not auto-trust MCP tools by capability.
- Surface prompts as slash commands /mcp**server**prompt in the command palette (args space-separated, mapped to the prompt's declared argument names) and resources as @server:protocol://path @-mentions with autocomplete fed from a cached resources/list; back them with read-only list/read tools and persist binary resource blobs to disk with a path reference rather than inlining base64.
- Support elicitation as a queued, modal-but-non-blocking request with form and url variants (url: open browser, then a 'Skip confirmation'/retry affordance keyed to an elicitationId and a completion signal), and expose a hook/automation point to auto-respond or decline before showing UI. Only advertise elicitation capability if AGI's client actually handles it.
- CLI parity: provide `agi mcp add --transport <stdio|http|sse> [--scope local|project|user] [--env K=V] [--header H] <name> -- <cmd...>` plus add-json, add-from-claude-desktop, list, get, remove, serve, and reset-project-choices, enforcing the 'all flags before the server name, then --' ordering rule. Support env-var expansion (${VAR}, ${VAR:-default}) in .mcp.json command/args/env/url/headers, and accept streamable-http as an alias for http.
- Mirror the context-budget behavior: defer MCP tool schemas by default (load names only), honor an alwaysLoad server/tool flag for tools needed every turn, and warn/cap large tool outputs (configurable max, persist-to-disk over threshold). Reflect 'always-loaded' vs 'deferred' status in the /mcp panel so users understand context cost.

**Conflicts (docs vs local reference)**

- Scope count: official docs headline THREE user-facing scopes (local/project/user) and describe enterprise/managed and claude.ai as separate layers, with no mention of a 'dynamic' scope; the source enum ConfigScopeSchema (types.ts:10-20) defines SEVEN (local, user, project, dynamic, enterprise, claudeai, managed). Resolution: the CODE wins for what AGI must model internally (all seven can appear -- e.g. claudeai connectors and managed/enterprise policy servers), while the DOCS' 3-scope framing wins as the user-facing mental model for the add/--scope UI.
- 'Local' overloading: both docs and code distinguish 'local scope' servers (stored in ~/.claude.json under the project path) from 'local settings' (approval state in .claude/settings.local.json). No true contradiction -- a naming hazard the upstream docs explicitly warn about; AGI must keep them as two separate stores so it doesn't silently write approval state into server config or vice versa.
- Provenance split (agreement, not contradiction): the full claude mcp add flag set (--transport/--scope/--env/--header/--callback-port/--client-id/--client-secret) and the canonical add/list/get/remove command surface come from the official docs page; the local handler file cli/handlers/mcp.tsx only implements add-json, add-from-claude-desktop, remove, list, get, serve, and reset-project-choices. Flag-level detail is sourced from docs; handler existence/behavior from code. They agree where they overlap.

## Claude Code CLI input/composer UX (Ink/React PromptInput) for AGI Rust/Ratatui ChatComposer

> Provenance note: every source for this section is inlined directly into the prose and key-findings below (each finding is prefixed with its `[src: ...]` path). There is no separate `sources[]` table for this entry.

<a id="claude-input-ux"></a>

Claude Code's composer is the PromptInput Ink/React tree. One text buffer drives everything; submit branches on whether the agent is busy. Source: /Users/siddhartha/Desktop/claude_reference/src/utils/handlePromptSubmit.ts (source-code, accessed 2026-06-01) shows that when a turn is active, Enter does not block or send; it enqueues the input (only prompt and bash modes are queueable) into a shared command queue and clears the box; interruptible tools abort the turn on submit; the idle path runs executeUserInput so direct and queued input share one loop. Queued items render as dim preview rows (cap 3 for notifications with a plus-N-more overflow) per /Users/siddhartha/Desktop/claude_reference/src/components/PromptInput/PromptInputQueuedCommands.tsx and drain FIFO. Multiline per /Users/siddhartha/Desktop/claude_reference/src/hooks/useTextInput.ts handleEnter: bare Enter submits; trailing backslash plus Enter, Shift Enter, or Meta Enter insert a newline (Apple Terminal native-shift fallback); the editor is full Emacs (Ctrl-A E B F K U W, Ctrl-Y yank, Meta-Y yank-pop, Meta-B F D), double-Esc clears saving to history, Ctrl-D exits when empty. Paste per /Users/siddhartha/Desktop/claude_reference/src/hooks/usePasteHandler.ts is bracketed, chunk-buffered with a 100ms timeout, image-path and macOS-screenshot aware; companion inputPaste.ts truncates text over 10000 chars to a Pasted-text reference and history.ts formats Pasted-text and Image refs expanded at submit. @ per /Users/siddhartha/Desktop/claude_reference/src/hooks/useTypeahead.ts opens a prewarmed git-ignore-aware file index typeahead merged with slash commands; Tab or Right-Arrow completes (dirs trailing slash, files trailing space), quoted at-paths support spaces, and the IDE pushes at-path line-range mentions. History is per-mode with Ctrl-R reverse search. The mode glyph per /Users/siddhartha/Desktop/claude_reference/src/components/PromptInput/PromptInputModeIndicator.tsx is a pointer for prompt and a colored bang for bash, derived from a leading bang in the buffer (inputModes.ts). AGI already has a Rust port of this queue at /Users/siddhartha/Desktop/agiworkforce/apps/cli/src/message_queue.rs (lanes Now/Next/Later, FIFO, cap 100). All findings are from the decompiled local source snapshot (files dated approx 2026-03-31, full TS recovered from embedded sourcemaps); the task screenshot dir claude-artifacts was empty (only Gemini and Codex CLI screenshots exist), so no Claude CLI screenshot corroboration was available.

**Key findings**

- [src: handlePromptSubmit.ts + PromptInputQueuedCommands.tsx] Submit is state-dependent and never blocking: bare Enter sends when idle, but while the agent is responding it ENQUEUES the typed text (only prompt and bash modes are queueable) into a shared FIFO priority queue, clears the box, and shows pending text as a dim preview row (notifications cap at 3 with a plus-N-more overflow) that drains when the turn ends; submitting during an interruptible tool aborts the turn instead.
- [src: hooks/useTextInput.ts handleEnter] Multiline is keyboard-explicit: bare Enter submits while trailing backslash plus Enter, Shift Enter, or Meta Enter insert a literal newline; Claude special-cases Apple Terminal because it cannot bind Shift Enter, so AGI on crossterm must choose a newline chord plus the universally-safe trailing-backslash fallback.
- [src: hooks/usePasteHandler.ts + inputPaste.ts + history.ts] Paste is buffered, classified, and dereferenced: bracketed chunks accumulate over a 100ms timeout, text over 10000 chars collapses to a Pasted-text reference (body stashed, re-expanded at submit), clipboard and dragged images (incl. macOS temp screenshots) become Image refs, and a same-tick paste-plus-Enter race is guarded. This reference-and-expand pattern is the highest-leverage feature to copy.
- [src: hooks/useTypeahead.ts + fileSuggestions.ts] @ is a first-class file picker distinct from slash commands and agent at-name DMs, all merged into one footer typeahead; typing @ queries a prewarmed git-ignore-aware file index, Tab or Right-Arrow completes, directories get a trailing slash and files a trailing space, quoted at-paths handle spaces, and a host or IDE can inject at-path line-range mentions; Enter is suppressed while a non-directory suggestion is open.
- [src: PromptInputModeIndicator.tsx + inputModes.ts] Mode is derived from the buffer, not a toggle: a leading bang selects bash mode and swaps the prompt glyph from a pointer to a colored bang, a single styled leading character that dims while the agent is responding.
- [src: useArrowKeyHistory.tsx + useHistorySearch.ts + useTextInput.ts + useInputBuffer.ts] History is per-mode and dual-modal: Up and Down walk prior inputs filtered by current mode (bash vs prompt) plus Ctrl-R opens a reverse-search dialog, double-Esc clears but first saves to history, and the editor is a full Emacs line editor with a debounced undo buffer.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- Wire ChatComposer submit into the EXISTING /Users/siddhartha/Desktop/agiworkforce/apps/cli/src/message_queue.rs lanes rather than building a new queue: enqueue at Next priority on Enter while a turn is active, render pending text as a dim preview row, drain FIFO on completion, and treat submit during an interruptible tool as abort-current-turn.
- Adopt the paste-reference pattern from inputPaste.ts: on paste over a threshold (Claude uses 10000 chars) replace the body in the visible buffer with a Pasted-text token and stash real content in a side map, expanding tokens and Image refs only at submit so the Ratatui textarea stays fast regardless of paste size.
- Build one unified typeahead (mirroring useTypeahead.ts), not three: switch source on the leading trigger (slash for commands, @ for file and dir index, at-name for agents), make Tab and Right-Arrow the accept key, reserve Enter for submit, complete dirs with a trailing slash and files with a trailing space, support quoted at-paths, back it with a prewarmed gitignore-aware file index, and support the at-path line-range form for editor or IDE injection.
- Make the prompt mode a derived single-glyph gutter (mirroring PromptInputModeIndicator.tsx): leading bang selects bash mode with a colored bang glyph otherwise the pointer, driven by the buffer string not a stored toggle, dimmed while responding, using palette tokens not hardcoded colors per the repo rule.
- Implement per-mode history (Up and Down filtered by bash vs prompt) plus a Ctrl-R reverse-search overlay and double-Esc clear-but-save-to-history, paired with a debounced undo buffer and core Emacs bindings (Ctrl-A E B F K U W, Ctrl-Y yank).
- Decide the AGI newline chord early with the always-works trailing-backslash-plus-Enter fallback and a one-line footer hint, and centralize the composer code from tui_app.rs and pane_view.rs into a dedicated ChatComposer widget mirroring PromptInput (interactive.rs is only list and tab pickers, not the text editor).

**Conflicts (docs vs local reference)**

- No conflicts between official docs and local reference code were found: the decompiled local source is the product itself and is authoritative for composer internals (truncation threshold 10000, kill-ring, queue lanes), so an empty conflicts set is the honest result. Provenance caveat: findings are from a local source snapshot dated approx 2026-03-31 (original TS recovered from embedded sourcemaps), and the task's claude-artifacts screenshot dir was empty, so there is no screenshot corroboration.

## Codex CLI TUI architecture: event loop, frame scheduling, app/bottom-pane/history wiring for AGI's Rust/Ratatui CLI

<a id="codex-tui-arch"></a>

Codex TUI is a single-threaded Ratatui app. App::run is one tokio select loop over four sources: internal AppEvents over mpsc, agent events, terminal TuiEvents, and app-server events, drawing only on Draw/Resize. A cloneable FrameRequester feeds a FrameScheduler actor that coalesces redraws into one broadcast draw tick capped at 120 FPS by FrameRateLimiter. TuiEventStream merges that draw broadcast with one shared crossterm EventBroker that can drop and recreate to release stdin for external programs, round-robining draw versus input. The Tui wrapper renders an inline viewport and writes finalized output to terminal scrollback via insert_history_lines inside a stdout sync_update. ChatWidget owns BottomPane (a composer plus a stack of modal/popup views) and the active cell; only active cell plus bottom pane render live as a FlexRenderable, while finalized HistoryCells become AppEvent InsertHistoryCell, stay in transcript_cells for the overlay, and are converted to lines handed to insert_history_lines.

**Key findings**

- Decouple request-a-redraw from render-a-frame: a cloneable FrameRequester plus a coalescing FrameScheduler actor emits one broadcast draw tick per ~8.33ms at a 120 FPS cap, so any widget or background task can call schedule_frame safely.
- One ownership-friendly event loop: a single tokio select multiplexes the AppEvent mpsc, the merged terminal/draw stream, agent events, and a backend channel; the TUI never blocks on the agent and draws only on Draw/Resize.
- Two-tier history is load-bearing: render only the active cell plus bottom pane in a small inline viewport, write every finalized cell to terminal scrollback via insert_history_lines so the OS terminal owns scroll/copy/select, and keep transcript_cells only for the overlay.
- Route terminal input through one shared crossterm source wrapped for drop/recreate via EventBroker pause/resume so external editors/pagers run without stealing stdin; round-robin polling prevents starvation.
- The bottom pane is a composer plus a stack of modal views (approvals, selection lists, popups) that replace the composer; input routes to the active view while interrupt/quit escalate to the parent, matching AGI's new approval_broker.rs and pane_view.rs.
- Render atomicity: each frame draws inside a synchronized terminal update so partial frames never flicker; viewport height comes from desired_height(width) and the cursor is set explicitly via cursor_pos, all exposed as one Renderable trait.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- Add a FrameRequester equivalent in apps/cli/src/tui: a cloneable handle backed by an mpsc-to-actor coalescer rate-limited to ~120 FPS; hand a clone to every widget (bottom pane, cost HUD, shimmer) instead of letting them trigger draws directly. Highest-leverage change for smooth animation without burning CPU.
- Refactor the 106KB tui_app.rs loop into one tokio select over an mpsc AppEvent channel, a merged TuiEvent stream (input + draw broadcast), the agent stream, and the approval broker; draw only on Draw/Resize and convert direct redraw calls into schedule_frame. The new app_event.rs and approval_broker.rs suggest this is already in flight.
- Adopt the inline-viewport plus scrollback split: render only the active streaming cell and bottom pane into a height-bounded viewport, commit finished turns to scrollback via an insert_history_lines path, and keep transcript_cell.rs cells in a vector for a Ctrl-T transcript overlay only.
- Wrap crossterm input in a pause/resume broker that drops and recreates the EventStream so AGI can shell out to an editor, pager, or local-model setup without stealing stdin; restore terminal modes around it and flush the input buffer on return, like Codex with_restored.
- Model the bottom pane as a composer plus a view-stack of modal popups (approvals, model/provider pickers, selection lists) with input routed to the top view and only interrupt/quit/submit bubbling to the parent; route approval decisions back through the AppEvent mpsc, not direct mutation. Reusable for AGI's local/BYOK provider-switch consent UI.
- Draw each frame inside a synchronized terminal update and recompute viewport height from a single Renderable trait (render, desired_height, cursor_pos); set the cursor explicitly to avoid flicker as the viewport grows and shrinks with multi-line input.
- Keep the loop single-threaded: all UI state behind mut self in the event-loop task while background work runs in spawned tasks reporting back only via the AppEvent mpsc, avoiding shared-mutex UI state and matching Codex's design.

**Conflicts (docs vs local reference)**

- No conflict found between Codex's local source and official docs. The FrameScheduler follows the Actors-with-Tokio pattern (ryhl.io, cited in frame_requester.rs) and the pause/resume stdin handling follows the Ratatui spawn-vim recipe (cited in event_stream.rs); these are patterns the code implements, not contradictions. Where Codex extends beyond the docs (120 FPS coalescing limiter, EventBroker drop/recreate to release stdin, sync_update atomic frames, inline-viewport-to-scrollback history) the local source wins as authoritative tested behavior because it encodes concrete fixes for the stdin-stealing race and flicker. No fast-moving API/version claim is asserted, so WebSearch/WebFetch/context7 were not loaded; the tokio/crossterm/ratatui APIs used are stable and proven by the in-tree code.

## Codex CLI approval overlay (queue/render/resolve) vs AGI approval_broker.rs, for a Rust/Ratatui CLI

<a id="codex-approval"></a>

Codex splits approval into TWO layers: a stateless VIEW (`ApprovalOverlay`, a `BottomPaneView` wrapping `ListSelectionView`) that holds an internal LIFO `Vec` queue of `ApprovalRequest`s and emits each user decision as an `AppCommand`/`AppEvent` op that round-trips to the agent thread (`exec_approval`/`patch_approval`/`resolve_elicitation`) — it never holds a per-request channel; and a SCHEDULING layer in `bottom_pane/mod.rs` (`push_approval_request` + `delayed_approval_requests` VecDeque) that delays showing the modal for 1s after composer typing and coalesces multiple requests into one overlay. AGI's `approval_broker.rs` is the inverse shape: a stateful async transport — a per-turn `ApprovalBroker` holding `Arc<Mutex<{ pending: VecDeque (true FIFO), responders: HashMap<Uuid, oneshot::Sender>, deny_all: bool }>>` plus an `Arc<Notify>`; tool code calls `broker.request(req).await` which suspends the tokio task on a `oneshot` until the UI calls `complete(id, decision)`. Contrary to a first scoped grep, AGI's broker is FULLY WIRED (not orphaned): `tui_app.rs` constructs a fresh broker per turn, installs it as an `ApprovalCallback` on `session.on_tool_approval`, and drives it via `tokio::select! { biased; turn_future; broker.notified() => drain_pending -> run_tui_approval_modal -> complete }`, with a separate `ApprovalOverlayState` widget rendering the prompt. Both designs are non-blocking to the render loop, but Codex decouples decision delivery through a protocol-op bus while AGI couples it through an in-memory responder map suspended on a tokio task. Note: the git-tracked `approval_broker.rs` blob initially read (211 lines, no Notify/deny_all) is STALE vs the on-disk file (295 lines), which is the version actually wired in.

**Key findings**

- Two-layer vs one-layer. Codex separates a stateless VIEW (ApprovalOverlay, holds queue + emits ops) from a SCHEDULER (bottom_pane: delay/coalesce). AGI fuses transport into one stateful broker and renders via a standalone modal function. AGI has a parallel PaneStack/PaneView scaffold (pane_view.rs) that mirrors Codex's BottomPaneView but is not yet used for approvals.
- Decision delivery is the core architectural divergence. Codex's overlay holds NO channel — it sends ReviewDecision as an AppCommand op (exec*approval/patch_approval/resolve_elicitation) that round-trips through the protocol bus to the agent thread; the overlay is fire-and-forget. AGI holds a per-request oneshot::Sender in a HashMap<Uuid,*> and the worker tokio task is literally suspended on rx.await until complete() fires. Codex's model scales naturally to cross-thread/multi-agent approvals (each op carries a ThreadId); AGI's in-memory map is single-process/per-turn.
- Non-blocking mechanism differs. Codex: overlay lives in a view_stack the single render loop already paints every frame; no task is suspended. AGI: the render loop would deadlock (worker awaits a decision a frozen UI can't deliver) WITHOUT the explicit tokio::select!{biased; turn_future; broker.notified()} in tui_app.rs L2661-2692 — the broker uses Arc<Notify> so the UI parks instead of busy-polling, and notify_one stores a permit so a request enqueued between drains is never lost.
- Queue ordering: easy to state backwards. Codex's overlay-internal queue is LIFO (Vec push/pop); FIFO _display_ order is reconstructed by the caller draining delayed_approval_requests with pop_back into enqueue_request. AGI's broker is genuinely FIFO (VecDeque push_back/pop_front). Same observable order, opposite internal mechanics.
- Codex has richer UX affordances AGI lacks: (a) a 1s post-typing delay before popping a modal so an approval doesn't interrupt mid-keystroke; (b) per-request silent dismissal (dismiss_resolved_request) when another thread/server already answered, WITHOUT emitting a spurious abort; (c) action-specific option sets and dynamic labels (network host, exec-policy prefix, per-session, strict-auto-review) driven by available_decisions; (d) a hard invariant that Esc==Cancel for MCP elicitation even under custom keymaps. AGI's broker has only complete (one decision) and cancel_all/deny_all_remaining (all-or-nothing); choices are a fixed Yes/AlwaysAllow/No/DenyAll set.
- AGI ALREADY has a feature Codex models differently: per-turn 'Deny All'. AGI latches deny_all in broker state so all remaining+future requests this turn auto-Cancel without prompting; a fresh broker per turn resets it. Codex achieves 'don't ask again' per-command/per-session/per-prefix through ReviewDecision variants persisted server-side, not a turn-scoped UI latch.
- Source-of-truth hazard observed: the git working-tree copy of approval_broker.rs first read (211 lines) lacked Notify/deny_all and looked orphaned; the actual on-disk file is 295 lines and is the wired version. Any audit reading the tracked blob alone would mis-conclude the broker is unused.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- Do NOT 'fix' the broker as orphaned — it is live (tui_app.rs L2645-2698). The real gap is that approvals bypass AGI's own PaneStack/PaneView abstraction (pane_view.rs) and run through a bespoke blocking modal loop (run_tui_approval_modal) that takes over the whole frame with Clear. To reach Codex parity, promote the approval prompt to a PaneView pushed on PaneStack so it composes with other overlays and is painted by the normal render loop, instead of a nested synchronous event::read() loop.
- Adopt Codex's typing-idle delay: add an APPROVAL_PROMPT_TYPING_IDLE_DELAY (~1s) so a request arriving mid-keystroke is queued and shown after the user pauses, rather than yanking focus. AGI's broker already buffers via VecDeque+Notify, so this is a UI-timing add, not a transport change.
- Add per-request silent dismissal (mirror dismiss_resolved_request): if a request is resolved out-of-band (e.g., a tool cancelled, parallel subagent answered), drop just that entry and wake its oneshot with the real outcome WITHOUT forcing Cancel on siblings. Today AGI can only cancel_all or deny_all_remaining (all-or-nothing) — too coarse once multi-tool/parallel turns land.
- Make options action-specific like Codex's exec_options/patch_options/permissions_options. AGI's ApprovalRequestKind already carries 10 variants (Exec/FileWrite/FileEdit/Patch/McpElicitation/Hook/Subagent/TrustDirectory/AskUser/LoopDetection) but the modal offers a fixed Yes/AlwaysAllow/No/DenyAll; derive per-kind labels and a per-kind allowed-decision set (e.g., 'allow this command for session', 'don't ask again for these files', host-scoped network grants).
- Enforce Codex's safety invariant for any future MCP-elicitation prompt: Esc must always map to Cancel (a safe abort), never silently to 'continue without info', even if keybindings are customized. AGI's ApprovalDecision has both Deny and Cancel; keep dismissal == Cancel and make that a tested contract.
- Consider migrating decision delivery toward Codex's op-bus model IF AGI moves to multi-thread/multi-agent turns. The current oneshot-per-request map is correct for single-process per-turn execution, but Codex carries ThreadId on every approval op precisely to route cross-thread approvals and open the source thread (open_thread shortcut). Tag requests with an originating-agent/thread id now so the broker doesn't need a rewrite later.
- Protect against the stale-blob trap: the version of approval_broker.rs that is wired (295 lines) differs from the git-tracked blob (211 lines). Commit the working-tree changes (Notify/deny_all_remaining/is_deny_all) or audits will keep mis-reading the broker as a no-op. Verify with a bare crate-wide `grep -rn ApprovalBroker apps/cli/src`, not a path-scoped grep, since the production construction lives in tui_app.rs not tui/ or tools/.

## Codex CLI `ChatComposer` (codex-rs TUI bottom pane) — feature map for AGI's CLI ChatComposer

<a id="codex-composer"></a>

Codex's ChatComposer is a bottom-pane input state machine combining two sub-machines: a UI-mode machine (`ActivePopup::{None,Command,File,Skill}`, at most one visible) and a non-bracketed paste-burst detector (`PasteBurst`). It wraps a multiline `TextArea` whose buffer carries inline "text element" placeholders for attachments and completed slash commands. `handle_key_event` routes keys to a popup handler when a popup is open, else to `handle_key_event_without_popup`; after every key it runs `sync_popups()` to reconcile popup visibility against text+cursor (verified in chat_composer.rs:1548, 2965, 3404). It supports slash-command popup (`/`), `@` file-search popup (async results via `AppEvent::StartFileSearch`), skill/app mention popup, Up/Down history recall split between persistent text-only `~/.codex/history.jsonl` and full-fidelity local session history, Ctrl+R reverse incremental search, large-paste collapsing to placeholders (>1000 chars), image-path paste attachment, `!` bash mode, Tab-to-queue while a task runs, and feature gating via `ChatComposerConfig`. AGI's current CLI composer is a single-line `String`+`usize` cursor in `tui_app.rs` (input:116, cursor:117) with a basic `show_slash_popup` flag and Up/Down bound to transcript scrolling — it has none of multiline editing, text-element placeholders, `@` file search, history recall, paste-burst, or queued input.

**Key findings**

- Two-machine architecture: ChatComposer is a UI-mode machine (ActivePopup::{None,Command,File,Skill}, exactly one popup at a time) plus a paste-burst detector. handle_key_event routes to the active popup first, else to handle_key_event_without_popup, then ALWAYS calls sync_popups() to reconcile popup state against the latest text+cursor. This 'route-then-sync' pattern is the central invariant (chat_composer.rs:1548,2965,3404).
- Multiline editing rides on a TextArea that stores inline 'text element' placeholders, not just a String. Elements represent attachments (`[Image #N]`), large-paste blobs, and completed slash commands — they render distinctly and edit atomically. Enter submits; a separate insert-newline key adds `\n`. The textarea kill-ring (Ctrl+K cut / Ctrl+Y yank) is deliberately preserved across submit and slash-dispatch so a user can kill text, run a composer action, then yank it back. All cursor-based slicing must clamp to UTF-8 char boundaries (doc:322-329).
- Slash popup: typing `/` at byte 0 of line 1 opens CommandPopup with fuzzy filtering; availability is centralized in slash_commands.rs and shared with the composer so gating never drifts. When the command name completes and the user types space, the `/command` token is promoted into an atomic text element. Commands dispatch as InputResult::Command or CommandWithArgs (args reuse the full submission-prep path so pasted content/elements survive). Built-ins are feature-gated (collaboration, connectors, plugins, fast, goal, personality, realtime, audio, elevate-sandbox) and side-conversation-gated.
- File search: `@token` (current_at_token, chat_composer.rs:2268) opens an async FileSearchPopup. The composer emits AppEvent::StartFileSearch(query); the popup tracks pending_query vs display_query with a `waiting` flag and discards stale results when query!=pending_query — classic debounced-async-search with last-write-wins. Bare `@` shows a hint ('set_empty_prompt'); states are 'loading...' / 'no matches'. A separate mention popup (current_mention_token) handles skill/app `$name` mentions with hidden path linkage distinct from `@` file search.
- History is two-tier: persistent cross-session (`~/.codex/history.jsonl`, text-only, no elements/attachments) + local in-session (full payload: text, element ranges, local image paths, remote image URLs, pending large-paste payloads). Up/Down recall on a non-empty draft only triggers when text matches the last recalled entry AND cursor is at a boundary (preserves multiline navigation). Ctrl+R is an incremental reverse search where the footer becomes the query field and the body previews the match; Enter accepts as editable draft, Esc restores the pre-search draft. Ctrl+C stashes the full draft into local history so Up restores it.
- Paste handling is dual-path: (a) bracketed paste → handle_paste(String); (b) non-bracketed bursts (Windows/VS Code terminals deliver paste as rapid Char+Enter key events) → PasteBurst buffers them into one explicit handle_paste. Burst detector only acts on plain chars (no Ctrl/Alt), holds the first ASCII char briefly to suppress flicker, never holds the first non-ASCII char (IME would feel dropped), and uses a 'looks pastey' heuristic (whitespace/length) before retro-grabbing IME prefixes. During a burst, Enter appends `\n` instead of submitting, and `?` cannot toggle the shortcut overlay. disable_paste_burst is an escape hatch that flushes in-flight state. Constants: MIN_CHARS=3, ENTER_SUPPRESS=120ms, CHAR_INTERVAL 8ms/30ms (non-win/win), IDLE_TIMEOUT 8ms/60ms (non-win/win).
- Large/image paste: pastes >1000 chars (LARGE_PASTE_CHAR_THRESHOLD) collapse to a placeholder element with the full text held in pending_pastes, expanded back to full text on submit. Smaller pastes that look like an image path attach the image (when image_paste_enabled) and insert a trailing space. CRLF is normalized to LF on every paste. image_paste_enabled is toggled at runtime by ChatWidget based on the model's input_modalities, with re-checks at attach/submit that warn rather than silently drop.
- Queued input + bash mode: leading `!` enters bash mode (the `!` is stripped, is_bash_mode set) and submission becomes QueuedInputAction::RunShell. Tab queues input while a task is running and submits like Enter when idle (so input is never dropped); Tab does NOT submit when the line starts with `!`. InputResult::Queued carries a QueuedInputAction (Plain/ParseSlash/RunShell). Submission flows through prepare_submission_text which expands pending pastes, trims + rebases element ranges, prunes attachments whose placeholders didn't survive trimming, and suppresses empty submissions.
- Reusability is built in: ChatComposerConfig gates popups_enabled / slash_commands_enabled / image_paste_enabled, with a plain_text() preset that turns the composer into a simple notes field — the same widget is reused across multiple bottom-pane surfaces. Remote image attachments render as non-editable `[Image #N]` rows above the textarea with their own Up/Down selection + Delete/Backspace removal, and numbering stays contiguous across remote+local images.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- Sequence the build to mirror Codex's dependency order; each stage unlocks the next. AGI starts from a single-line String+cursor (tui_app.rs:116-117), so the foundation must come first.
- STAGE 1 — Multiline TextArea abstraction. Replace the `input: String` + `cursor: usize` with a dedicated TextArea type supporting `\n`, per-line cursor movement, and UTF-8-boundary-clamped slicing. Add inline 'text element' placeholders from day one (even if only used for slash-command tokens initially) — retrofitting elements later is expensive because every paste/history/submit path depends on them. Bind Enter=submit and a distinct key (e.g. Shift+Enter or Ctrl+J) = insert newline; add Ctrl+K kill / Ctrl+Y yank with a kill-ring preserved across submit.
- STAGE 2 — Promote slash popup to the route-then-sync model. AGI's popup opens only when input=='/' exactly (tui_app.rs:1058). Adopt Codex's pattern: a single sync_popups() called after every key that recomputes popup visibility from text+cursor, fuzzy-filters commands, and promotes the completed `/cmd ` token into an atomic element. Centralize command availability/gating in one module shared by the popup and the dispatcher (mirror slash_commands.rs) so the two never drift.
- STAGE 3 — `@` file search. Add an `@token` detector and an async, debounced FileSearchPopup: emit a StartFileSearch app-event, track pending vs displayed query, and drop stale results (last-write-wins). This is the single biggest UX feature AGI lacks vs Codex and is high-value for a coding CLI. Reuse the same popup scroll/selection primitives as the slash popup.
- STAGE 4 — Paste-burst detector. Port PasteBurst as a standalone module. Even on macOS/Linux (AGI's primary targets per India-first GTM), bracketed paste can be unreliable in some terminals; the burst detector prevents mid-paste submission and `?`-overlay flicker. Use Codex's platform-gated constants (8ms char interval / 8ms idle on non-Windows; 30ms/60ms on Windows; MIN_CHARS=3; ENTER_SUPPRESS=120ms) and the ASCII-hold / non-ASCII-no-hold IME distinction. Add a disable_paste_burst escape hatch. Also add large-paste collapsing to a placeholder (Codex threshold 1000 chars) — critical for a CLI where users paste logs/diffs.
- STAGE 5 — History recall + Ctrl+R. Move Up/Down off transcript-scroll (current tui_app.rs:1120-1121 behavior) onto shell-style input-history recall, gated on cursor-at-boundary so multiline navigation still works. Split persistent (text-only on-disk JSONL) from local session history (full draft state) to stay disk-backward-compatible while giving rich in-session recall. Add Ctrl+R reverse incremental search with a footer query field and body preview. Stash the draft on Ctrl+C so Up restores it.
- STAGE 6 — Queued input + bash mode. Add a queued-submission path (Tab queues while a task runs, submits when idle, never drops input) and a leading-`!` bash/shell mode. Model the result as a typed enum (Plain / ParseSlash / RunShell) like Codex's InputResult+QueuedInputAction so the dispatcher stays explicit. Note: AGI's locked product rules keep this LOCAL-only — ensure RunShell routes through AGI's existing bash tool approval/sandbox path, never to a remote provider.
- Cross-cutting: adopt ChatComposerConfig-style feature gating (popups/slash/image flags + a plain_text preset) so the composer can be reused for other AGI bottom-pane inputs (approval prompts, elicitation) without forking the widget. Keep all colors on AGI's Ratatui palette tokens per the project's no-hardcoded-colors rule — do not copy any literal styling from Codex.
- Pin behavior with integration tests the way Codex does (burst-handles-newline, question-mark-no-toggle-during-burst, large-paste-placeholder, at-token boundary cases). Codex exercises PasteBurst through ChatComposer integration tests rather than unit tests — the same approach fits AGI's harness and catches the cross-cutting sync_popups invariants.

**Conflicts (docs vs local reference)**

- Tab-queue conditionality — doc vs code; CODE WINS. docs/tui-chat-composer.md:102-108 frames queuing as gated: 'When steer mode is enabled, Tab requests queuing if a task is already running... Enter always submits immediately in this mode.' But the source shows steer mode was removed: set_steer_enabled is a #[cfg(test)] no-op shim explicitly commented 'Compatibility shim for tests that still toggle the removed steer mode flag' (chat_composer.rs:747-749), and the module docstring (chat_composer.rs:41-43) states the Tab-queues-while-running / submits-when-idle behavior unconditionally. The OUTCOME is identical; only the doc's 'when steer mode is enabled / in this mode' qualifier is stale. Source code is authoritative because it is the executed behavior and the doc's gating flag no longer exists. For AGI this means: implement queue-while-running / submit-when-idle as always-on, not behind a mode toggle.
- No separate official product docs exist at this layer, by design — recorded so the omission is explicit, not silent. Composer internals (state machine, key routing, paste-burst timing) are implementation behavior whose ground truth is the Rust source itself; Codex's only 'docs' at this layer is the in-repo docs/tui-chat-composer.md, which was already consulted and cross-checked against the code. A web search would resolve to the same public GitHub repository and add no independent authority while consuming the 3-6 source budget, so it was intentionally not performed. Where the in-repo narrative doc and the source disagree (see the steer-mode item), the source wins.

## Codex CLI transcript/tool cell rendering (codex-rs/tui) mapped to AGI apps/cli transcript_cell.rs contract

<a id="codex-cells"></a>

Codex renders the conversation as a vector of concrete `HistoryCell` trait objects (~40 distinct struct types: UserHistoryCell, AgentMarkdownCell, ReasoningSummaryCell, ExecCell, McpToolCallCell, WebSearchCell, PatchHistoryCell, PlanUpdateCell, HookCell, etc.), each producing styled `Vec<Line<'static>>` rather than plain strings. The trait carries the compact-vs-expanded split as two render methods: `display_lines(width)` (truncated to TOOL_CALL_MAX_LINES=5 with a "… +N lines (ctrl+t to view transcript)" hint) and `transcript_lines(width)` (full output for the Ctrl+T overlay), each with its own row-aware height method. Streaming flows into a single in-flight `active_cell: Option<Box<dyn HistoryCell>>` on ChatWidget that mutates in place via `complete_call`/`append_output`/`with_added_call`, with a revision counter bumped on every mutation so the cached transcript tail invalidates; when an exec cell's calls all complete (`should_flush`) it is flushed into committed history. AGI's `transcript_cell.rs` is a not-yet-wired scaffold: a single `TranscriptCell` trait with a `TranscriptCellKind` enum (13 variants) + explicit `TranscriptCellState` enum, a `render_text(width) -> Vec<String>` (unstyled), and boolean `is_expandable`/`is_expanded` — but no expanded render path and no styling channel. The live AGI TUI still renders from `chat_messages: Vec<ChatMessage>` via Paragraph in tui_app.rs and never references the new cell contract. Codex's internal cell taxonomy is not a public API, so local source is the authoritative artifact for this target; no official docs apply.

**Key findings**

- RETURN-TYPE DIVERGENCE (biggest gap): AGI's `render_text(width) -> Vec<String>` returns unstyled strings (transcript_cell.rs:41); Codex's `display_lines(width) -> Vec<Line<'static>>` returns styled spans (history_cell.rs:115). Everything Codex's tool/exec rendering relies on — green/red status bullet, shimmer spinner, magenta `$`, dim ` └`/` │` gutters, DIM modifiers — is span-level style that AGI's current contract structurally cannot carry. AGI must move to styled lines (ratatui Line/Span) before it can match Codex visuals.
- COMPACT-VS-EXPANDED DIVERGENCE: Codex implements it with TWO render methods (`display_lines` = compact, truncated to TOOL_CALL_MAX_LINES=5 with a '… +N lines (ctrl + t to view transcript)' hint, via middle-truncation in exec_cell/render.rs; `transcript_lines` = full untruncated output) plus TWO height methods (`desired_height`/`desired_transcript_height`) feeding a global Ctrl+T overlay. AGI models it as per-cell booleans `is_expandable()`/`is_expanded()` — but `render_text(width)` takes no compact/expanded flag, so AGI's contract currently has NO render pathway for the expanded form. Incomplete contract, not just a stylistic difference.
- TAXONOMY DIVERGENCE: AGI uses one tagged trait — `TranscriptCellKind` enum (User/Assistant/Reasoning/Exec/Tool/Patch/Approval/Task/Subagent/Warning/Error/SystemNotice/Plan) + explicit `TranscriptCellState` enum (Pending/Running/Complete/Failed/Cancelled). Codex uses ~40 concrete structs each implementing HistoryCell, and carries NO explicit state enum — state is implicit (exec: `output.is_some()`, `exit_code==0`). AGI's explicit-state design is arguably cleaner for routing but diverges from Codex's type-per-cell approach.
- STREAMING-INTO-ACTIVE-CELLS: Codex keeps a single in-flight `active_cell: Option<Box<dyn HistoryCell>>` that mutates in place. Exec end events route by `call_id` into ActiveTracked / OrphanHistoryWhileActiveExec / NewCell (chatwidget.rs:4876); `complete_call` returning false is treated as a real routing-mismatch signal, not silently ignored (model.rs:82). Every in-place mutation bumps `active_cell_revision` so the Ctrl+T overlay's cached live tail invalidates. AGI's contract has no active-cell / call_id-routing / revision concept yet — its app_event.rs has ToolStarted/ToolUpdated/ToolCompleted with call_id, but transcript_cell.rs is immutable (build cell from text, no in-place append).
- EXEC 'EXPLORING' COALESCING has no AGI equivalent: Codex's ExecCell groups consecutive read-only commands (Read/ListFiles/Search) into one 'Exploring'/'Explored' cell, merging adjacent Read calls and de-duplicating filenames (exec_cell/render.rs:262, model.rs is_exploring_call:154). AGI's Exec/Tool kinds are flat 1-cell-per-call with no grouping logic.
- SCAFFOLD-NOT-LIVE: AGI's transcript_cell.rs (and pane_view.rs, app_event.rs, approval_broker.rs) are `#![allow(dead_code)]` scaffolds with zero production consumers; the live TUI still renders from `chat_messages: Vec<ChatMessage>` through Paragraph in tui_app.rs (render_chat at line 620). So the contract can be redesigned freely before wiring — evolve it first, wire second.
- PATCH RENDERING (verified, not assumed): Codex `PatchHistoryCell.display_lines` delegates to `diff_render::create_diff_summary` (history_cell.rs:1089), which builds per-file rows (added/removed counts derived from FileChange::Add/Delete content line counts or Update unified_diff), sorts by path, and emits a styled header per file: 'Added/Deleted/Edited <path> (+N -M)' with green `+N` / red `-M` (diff_render.rs:393-435), followed by a hunk block. AGI's `Patch` cell kind is only an enum tag with no diff/hunk renderer; AGI's render_text(Vec<String>) cannot reproduce the green/red counts.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- Change the core render method from `render_text(width) -> Vec<String>` to a styled-line return (ratatui `Vec<Line<'static>>`), mirroring Codex `display_lines`. Without this AGI cannot render status bullets, spinners, dim output gutters, or +N/-M diff counts. This is the prerequisite for every other tool/exec/patch visual.
- Add an explicit expanded render path. Either follow Codex (split into `display_lines` compact + `transcript_lines` full + matching height methods + a Ctrl+T-style overlay) or pass a compact/expanded flag into a single render method. The current `is_expandable`/`is_expanded` booleans have no render that honors them — close that gap before wiring.
- Introduce an active-cell + call_id routing model (port Codex's `active_cell: Option<Box<dyn TranscriptCell>>`, `complete_call`/`append_output` returning bool for mismatch detection, and a revision counter). AGI's app_event.rs already carries call_id on ToolStarted/Updated/Completed, so the event side is ready; the cell side needs in-place mutation instead of immutable text cells.
- Adopt Codex's truncation+hint pattern for tool/exec output: cap compact output at a small line budget (Codex uses 5 for tools, 50 for user shell), middle-truncate with a '… +N lines' hint pointing to the expanded view, and measure height in viewport rows (Paragraph::line_count with Wrap{trim:false}) so long URL-like tokens don't undercount. AGI's current wrap_line in transcript_cell.rs is a naive char-count wrap with no truncation or row-aware height.
- Build a real diff renderer for the Patch cell kind (per-file Added/Deleted/Edited header + green/red +N/-M summary + optional hunks), porting the shape of `diff_render::create_diff_summary`. The Patch enum variant is currently a label with no renderer.
- Decide consciously between AGI's enum-tagged single-trait design and Codex's struct-per-cell design before wiring. AGI's explicit `TranscriptCellState` is a genuine improvement over Codex's implicit state and worth keeping; pair it with concrete cell data structs (ExecCell-equivalent holding calls/output/duration) rather than the current PlainTranscriptCell-only approach, so Exec/Tool/Patch cells can carry structured data.
- Optionally port the exec 'exploring' coalescing (group consecutive Read/List/Search into one Explored cell) — it materially reduces transcript noise for agent file-exploration, which AGI's flat-per-call model lacks.
- Keep evolving the scaffold (transcript_cell.rs/app_event.rs/pane_view.rs/approval_broker.rs) before connecting it to tui_app.rs's live `chat_messages` path; the dead_code allowance means contract changes are free now and expensive after wiring.

**Conflicts (docs vs local reference)**

- No official-docs conflict applies: Codex's internal TUI cell taxonomy (HistoryCell trait, ExecCell, diff_render) is not a published/public API, so the local reference source at ~/Desktop/reference/codex-cli is the sole authoritative artifact for this target. The task's 'and/or official docs' permits local-source-only here; I deliberately consulted no external docs because none govern this internal contract. Local source therefore wins by default — there is nothing to reconcile against.

## AGI CLI TUI dialog/overlay system — PaneStack priority + settings panels (apps/cli/src/tui/pane_view.rs, approval_broker.rs)

<a id="gemini-dialogs"></a>

Gemini CLI does NOT stack dialogs — its DialogManager.tsx is a flat, priority-ordered SINGLE-SLOT chain of `if (cond) return <Dialog/>` branches, so the first truthy condition short-circuits and exactly one dialog renders at a time. Priority is encoded purely by source order, sequenced least-dismissable-first: admin-settings-changed → IDE-restart/new-agents → quota/validation/overage/empty-wallet → IDE-nudge/folder-trust/policy-update → loop-detection → permission/command/auth consent → extension-update → user-invoked config (theme/settings/model/voice/agent-config) → banned-account/auth-in-progress/api-key/auth-dialog → editor/privacy/session-browser/permissions. At the layout level there are three mutually-exclusive priority tiers: `customDialog` > `DialogManager` chain > `Composer` (input), gated by a single derived `dialogsVisible` boolean so dialogs and the input prompt never co-render. Keybindings are a data-driven Command-enum → KeyBinding[] map (defaults in keyBindings.ts) merged with an optional user `~/.gemini/keybindings.json` (VS Code-style `{command, key}` array, `-` prefix unbinds); matching is per-context (`keyMatchers[Command.X](key)`) not a single global map, so the same key (tab, ctrl+c) is reused across contexts. Settings are a typed schema with 4 scopes (User/Workspace/System/SystemDefaults) and per-setting `requiresRestart` flags; the SettingsDialog provides fzf search, an "Apply To" scope selector (Tab switches focus between settings list and scope), and restart-required diff tracking. This contrasts sharply with AGI's PaneStack, which is a literal LIFO `Vec<Box<dyn PaneView>>` routing input to `.last()` — last-pushed wins regardless of urgency.

**Key findings**

- PRIORITY, NOT STACKING: Gemini's DialogManager renders exactly ONE dialog via a flat ordered if/return chain (DialogManager.tsx). 'Stacking' from the task framing does not exist in Gemini — priority is the source order of the branches, sequenced least-dismissable/most-urgent first.
- THREE-TIER LAYOUT GATING: customDialog > DialogManager-chain > Composer, mutually exclusive via the single derived `dialogsVisible` OR-boolean (AppContainer.tsx:2188). The input prompt is fully replaced while any dialog is up — no focus ambiguity between input and modal.
- SEVERITY ORDERING IS THE REUSABLE PRINCIPLE: system/admin/trust/policy/quota dialogs sit ABOVE loop-detection and approval/consent, which sit above user-invoked config (theme/settings/model), which sits above auth flows. The user can never bury an urgent system prompt under a panel they opened.
- KEYBINDINGS ARE DATA-DRIVEN + PER-CONTEXT: Command enum → KeyBinding[] defaults (keyBindings.ts), merged with user keybindings.json (`{command,key}` array, `-` unbinds, additions prepended). Resolution is per-context via keyMatchers[Command.X](key), so the same physical key safely means different things in input vs dialog vs shell-focus (tab, ctrl+c reused).
- SETTINGS UX = TYPED SCHEMA + SCOPE SELECTOR + RESTART DIFF: SettingsDialog has fzf fuzzy search over setting keys, an 'Apply To' scope radio (User/Workspace/System), Tab to switch focus between the settings list and the scope selector, TOGGLE_TYPES for boolean settings, and a mount-time snapshot of requiresRestart settings to detect and prompt for restart on save (SettingsDialog.tsx, settingsSchema.ts).
- AGI'S PaneStack IS A DIFFERENT MODEL (LIFO): pane_view.rs routes input to the last-pushed view and pops on Close. Pure last-wins ordering means a casually-opened panel can mask a later urgent approval/trust/quota request — the exact failure Gemini's severity-ordered chain prevents.
- AGI ALREADY HAS THE HOOKS: PaneView::can_consume_approval() and requires_attention() in pane_view.rs mirror Gemini's 'active panel consumes approval before a separate overlay opens' and 'this dialog demands attention' semantics — the scaffolding for a priority resolver is present but unused.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- Split AGI's overlay system into TWO layers: a priority RESOLVER above the navigable PaneStack. System/security/approval dialogs (TrustDirectory, policy, quota, LoopDetection, Hook, Exec/FileWrite approvals from approval_broker.rs's ApprovalRequestKind) must be selected by SEVERITY ORDER and PREEMPT the user-navigable PaneStack — never be a peer entry that LIFO can bury. Mirror Gemini's DialogManager ordering: admin/trust/policy > quota > loop-detection > approval/consent > user-config panels > auth.
- Keep PaneStack (LIFO) only for user-invoked, freely-dismissable navigable panels (settings, theme, model picker, session browser). For everything that arrives unsolicited and is safety-relevant, route through the resolver, not push().
- Wire the existing PaneView::requires_attention() and can_consume_approval() hooks: when an ApprovalRequest arrives, first offer it to the active pane (can_consume_approval) — exactly Gemini's 'active panel consumes approval before opening a separate overlay' — and only if refused, surface a resolver-owned overlay. requires_attention() should let a backgrounded pane force itself to the top of the priority order.
- Adopt Gemini's three-tier mutual exclusion at render time: a single derived `dialogs_visible` (or `active_overlay`) that swaps the bottom region between a system/resolver overlay, the navigable PaneStack, and the composer/input — never render input concurrently with a modal that owns the keyboard. This kills focus-deadlock bugs.
- Model settings as a typed schema with explicit `scope` and `requires_restart` per key, not a flat blob. Build the settings panel with: fuzzy search over keys, a scope selector (machine-default/user/project, project overriding user), inline toggle for boolean types, and a restart-required diff that prompts on save — all directly from Gemini's SettingsDialog/settingsSchema pattern.
- Make keybindings data-driven: a Command enum → bindings map with a user-overridable keybindings file (`{command, key}`, `-` to unbind, user additions take precedence). Resolve per-context (an input-context matcher set vs a dialog-context matcher set) rather than one global table, so AGI can safely reuse keys (Esc, Tab, Ctrl+C) across input/dialog/shell focus like Gemini does.
- Do NOT copy Gemini's quota/wallet/overage/empty-wallet dialog branches — those are managed-cloud billing surfaces. Per AGI's v1 LOCAL-ONLY lock they have no analog; AGI's high-priority slots are trust/policy/approval/loop-detection only, which keeps the resolver chain shorter and the trust boundary clean.

**Conflicts (docs vs local reference)**

- Settings scope count: official docs (docs/cli/settings.md) describe only 2 scopes — User and Workspace, 'Workspace overrides User'. The local reference code (settings.ts:128-154 and the merge comment at 262-268) defines 4 scopes — User, Workspace, System, SystemDefaults — with precedence (last wins): defaults → SystemDefaults → User → Workspace → System-as-overrides. CODE WINS: the docs are a simplified user-facing subset; the code is the shipped behavior and additionally enforces that untrusted-workspace settings are dropped. For AGI, model 4 tiers (or at least machine-default/user/project) with project overriding user, but allow an admin/system tier that overrides project.
- Restart-required: docs (settings.md) do not enumerate which settings need a restart (only imply it for max-old-space-size). Code is authoritative: settingsSchema.ts attaches an explicit per-setting `requiresRestart: boolean` flag and SettingsDialog snapshots those at mount to prompt for restart on change. CODE WINS — treat requiresRestart as a first-class per-setting property, not an afterthought.
