## AGI ToolCell / tool-group rendering in apps/cli/src/tui/ (transcript_cell.rs, pane_view.rs) — porting Gemini CLI's grouped-tool message system to Rust/Ratatui. Gemini's reference target: /Users/siddhartha/Desktop/reference/gemini-cli/packages/cli/src/ui/components/messages/

<a id="gemini-tools"></a>

Gemini CLI renders a batch of tool calls as ONE continuous round-bordered container (not stacked separate boxes). ToolGroupMessage owns the box geometry: it filters hidden calls, groups consecutive Agent-kind calls into sub-arrays, then for each group emits a tool whose header is a sticky StickyHeader and whose result hangs directly below sharing the left/right borders. The box is stitched across tools by two booleans: isFirst toggles borderTop and showClosingBorder toggles borderBottom, both recomputed at every compact/topic/agent transition so the outline stays seamless. Each individual ToolMessage shows a status indicator (o pending, spinner executing, ✓ success, ? confirming, - canceled, x error), a bold tool name plus dim description truncated to one line, optional MCP progress bar, then ToolResultDisplay which type-switches on the result payload (pretty-JSON, markdown, file-diff, ANSI shell output array, structured summary, or raw object). Vertical space is budgeted: a computed staticHeight is subtracted from availableTerminalHeight and the remainder divided across only the tools that actually have output, and overflow is truncated with a hidden-lines label (top-overflow for normal tools, bottom-overflow for agent output). Subagents get their own SubagentGroupDisplay with an expand/collapse (ctrl+o) state and per-agent status icons.

**Key findings**

- CENTRAL EXTRACTION: a tool group is ONE continuous round-bordered container, not stacked boxes. The container outline is assembled per-tool from booleans: isFirst→borderTop, showClosingBorder→borderBottom; the header is a sticky box and the result body is a borderLeft+borderRight-only box directly beneath it so they read as one bordered cell. showClosingBorder is recomputed at every transition (compact→standard, topic, agent, last) so the seam never breaks. A Ratatui port should model this as 'group draws the box, each tool contributes top/bottom edges based on its position and neighbor types' rather than each tool drawing its own full border.
- Two portable algorithms a Ratatui port needs (these are layout math, not Ink-specific): (a) HEIGHT BUDGET — compute a fixed staticHeight (chrome: borders, separators, headers, output-file rows) then availableHeightPerTool = max(floor((availableTerminalHeight - staticHeight) / max(1, countToolsWithOutput)), 1); only tools whose resultDisplay is non-empty count toward the divisor. (b) OVERFLOW TRUNCATION — clamp result to the budget and show a hidden-lines count label; overflowDirection is 'top' for normal tools (keep the tail/newest) but 'bottom' for agent results (keep the head).
- Status model is richer than AGI's current TranscriptCellState. Gemini's display status set is {Pending, Executing, Success, Confirming, Canceled, Error}; Confirming comes from core AwaitingApproval and is a FIRST-CLASS in-band tool status (renders a '?' in the same header slot). AGI's TranscriptCellState (Pending/Running/Complete/Failed/Cancelled) has no Confirming/awaiting-approval state and instead models approval as a separate cell Kind (Approval) — a structural divergence to decide on deliberately.
- On-screen status glyphs (verified against the renderer, not the constant): o pending, animated spinner executing, ✓ success, ? confirming, - canceled, x error. The EXECUTING:'⊷' value in constants.ts is dead in this path — ToolStatusIndicator renders <CliSpinner type='toggle'/> for Executing. Colors are semantic-theme tokens (success/warning/error/active/focus), never literals.
- ToolResultDisplay is a single payload type-switch, NOT one renderer per tool. The result variant is chosen from the payload shape (pretty-JSON string, markdown string, {fileDiff}, ANSI line array for shell, {summary,payload} structured, raw object, todos→null). This means AGI's ToolCell body should branch on a result enum, decoupled from tool name; tool-name-specific compaction (DenseToolMessage allowlist) is a separate concern layered on top.
- Subagents are a distinct grouped view (SubagentGroupDisplay): consecutive Agent-kind calls collapse under one ≡ fleet-status header with an expand/collapse toggle (ctrl+o) registered into a global overflow/footer system. Collapsed = one status-icon + truncated-activity line per agent; expanded = full per-agent history. AGI already has a Subagent cell kind to host this.
- The rendering MECHANISM does not port. StickyHeader relies on this Ink fork's sticky/stickyChildren/opaque scrollback primitive, flexGrow/flexShrink flexbox, and an explicit width workaround documented as guarding an Ink border-tearing bug. Ratatui is immediate-mode with Constraint-based layout and has no sticky-scrollback header primitive — AGI must reproduce the 'header stays visible while body scrolls' effect with a fixed header pane or re-render-on-scroll, not by copying the sticky box.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- Make the tool GROUP, not the individual ToolCell, own the border geometry. In pane_view.rs, render a batch of tool cells inside one bordered region and have each cell report whether it needs a top edge (first / after a compact or topic cell) and a bottom edge (last / before a transition). Port Gemini's isFirst + showClosingBorder logic (ToolGroupMessage.tsx 344-484) as the seam rule so the outline stays continuous across mixed cell types.
- Add a height-budget pass to the transcript layout: compute fixed chrome height, subtract from the available rows, divide the remainder across only the cells that have output (mirror staticHeight + availableTerminalHeightPerToolMessage, ToolGroupMessage.tsx 182-299). Without this, one long tool result starves the others; Ratatui's Constraint::Min/Max can express the per-cell cap once the budget is computed.
- Implement overflow truncation with a visible hidden-lines label and a per-kind direction: keep the TAIL (overflow top) for normal tool/shell output, keep the HEAD (overflow bottom) for subagent output — exactly Gemini's overflowDirection split (ToolMessage.tsx 143, ToolResultDisplay.tsx). transcript_cell.rs already exposes is_expandable/is_expanded; wire ctrl+o expand to lift the cap.
- Decide deliberately whether the tool ToolCell needs an in-band Confirming/AwaitingApproval state. Gemini renders approval as a tool status ('?') in the header; AGI currently has a separate Approval cell Kind and an approval_broker.rs. Either add a Confirming variant to TranscriptCellState and render it in the tool header (closer to Gemini, fewer cells), or keep approvals as their own cell but ensure the owning tool cell visibly reflects 'awaiting approval' so the two stay in sync.
- Model the result body as an enum/type-switch (ToolResultDisplay pattern), not per-tool renderers: variants for PrettyJson, Markdown, FileDiff, AnsiShellLines, StructuredSummary, RawObject, and a None case (todos render elsewhere). Branch on payload shape, keeping tool-name-specific compaction (the DenseToolMessage allowlist) as an optional layer over the same enum.
- Build a real subagent group cell behind the existing Subagent kind: one ≡ fleet-status header ('Running N Agents...', 'N completed'), per-agent status icons (running/completed/cancelled/error), a truncated last-activity line per agent collapsed, full history expanded, and an expand/collapse toggle surfaced in the footer (mirror SubagentGroupDisplay + its overflow registration).
- Use semantic palette tokens for every status color (terminal*palette.rs), never literals — Gemini routes all of these through theme.status.* / theme.ui.\_ and AGI's no-hardcoded-colors rule requires the same. Map: success→✓/Complete, warning/active→Running+Confirming, error→Failed, plus the pending/canceled glyphs.
- Do NOT try to copy StickyHeader. Reproduce 'tool header stays visible while its output scrolls' with a Ratatui-native approach (fixed header line within the cell's allotted rect, or redraw-on-scroll), and verify the group border renders cleanly across state changes — Gemini documents an actual border-tearing bug it had to defend against (ToolGroupMessage.tsx 320-326), so add a snapshot test for rapidly-changing tool state.

**Conflicts (docs vs local reference)**

- No official-docs conflict applies: this is an internal-component source study and there is no public Gemini CLI documentation describing ToolGroupMessage's rendering internals, so the reference source code IS the authority and there is nothing for docs to contradict.
- Intra-source discrepancy worth flagging (resolved by reading the renderer): constants.ts:23 defines EXECUTING:'⊷', but ToolStatusIndicator (ToolShared.tsx 161-165) renders a CliSpinner for the Executing branch and never uses that glyph. The renderer wins — the on-screen executing indicator is the animated spinner, not ⊷.

## OpenCode TUI architecture (cli/cmd/tui + component/prompt + dialogs) — local reference v1.14.30, verified vs sst/opencode dev branch

<a id="opencode-tui"></a>

OpenCode's TUI is a TypeScript/TSX application built on SolidJS reactivity bound to OpenTUI (@opentui/solid + @opentui/core, a Zig/Yoga terminal renderer with a Bun FFI), NOT the older Go/Bubbletea TUI. The entry point tui()/App in app.tsx composes ~18 nested context providers (Args, KV, Toast, Route, SDK, Project, Sync, Theme, Local, Keybind, PromptStash, Dialog, Command, Frecency, PromptHistory, PromptRef, Editor) around two routes (Home, Session) plus a plugin route. State is SolidJS createStore/createSignal/createMemo; UI is JSX primitives (<box>, <text>, <textarea>, <scrollbox>) laid out with flexbox. A single command registry (dialog-command.tsx) feeds both the command palette and global keybinds, with each command carrying value/keybind/slash/category/suggested/hidden. The prompt (component/prompt/index.tsx) is a rich editor with a parts model (text/file/agent/paste) rendered as inline virtual-text "extmarks", @-mention and /-command autocomplete (fuzzysort + frecency), shell mode via leading '!', triple-esc interrupt, and paste summarization/image-PDF attachment. Dialogs are a modal stack (ui/dialog.tsx) that esc-pops one layer and refocuses the prior renderable; DialogSelect is the shared fuzzy-filtered, category-grouped, keyboard+mouse list used by most dialogs. Verified current vs the official sst/opencode dev branch via GitHub API; architecture is identical, with minor version drift (keybind module moved).

**Key findings**

- Stack is TSX + SolidJS + OpenTUI (Zig renderer), confirmed primarily by `@opentui/solid`/`@opentui/core` imports in app.tsx — the old Go/Bubbletea OpenCode TUI is fully replaced. UI primitives are JSX `<box>/<text>/<textarea>/<scrollbox>` with flexbox (Yoga) layout; state is createStore/createSignal/createMemo. For a Rust/Ratatui port the portable lesson is the structure, not the reactivity engine.
- Single command registry drives BOTH the palette and global keybinds (dialog-command.tsx). Each command is {title, value, keybind?, slash?, category, suggested?, hidden?, enabled?, onSelect(dialog)}. The same list yields: palette entries (DialogSelect), global keyboard shortcuts (useKeyboard matching option.keybind), and slash commands (slashes() with aliases). Registration is decentralized — App and Prompt each call command.register(() => [...]) and entries are reconciled reactively.
- Dialogs are a modal STACK with esc-pop + focus restoration (ui/dialog.tsx). Opening blurs and remembers currentFocusedRenderable; esc/ctrl+c pops exactly one layer, runs onClose, then refocus() walks the tree to re-focus the saved renderable. Three fixed widths (medium/large/xlarge). One translucent overlay at zIndex 3000; click-outside dismisses.
- DialogSelect is the reusable fuzzy-list primitive behind the palette and nearly every picker (model/agent/theme/session/skill/stash/etc.). Features: fuzzysort with title>category weighting, category grouping + headers, current-item dot, per-row keybind footers, left/right footer keybind hints, and a keyboard-vs-mouse input-mode flag that ignores hover events triggered by layout shift during filtering.
- The prompt is a structured editor, not a plain textbox. A parts array (text | file | agent | paste) is kept in sync with the visible buffer via OpenTUI 'extmarks' (virtual-text spans with style IDs). @mentions/files/agents and large pastes render as compact inline tokens ('[Image 1]', '[Pasted ~N lines]', '@file') but expand to full content/attachments at submit time. This is the trickiest pattern to port: it requires a parallel span model over the input buffer.
- Input modes and affordances: leading '!' enters shell mode (border turns primary, submit routes to session.shell, esc/backspace-at-0 exits); '/cmd' at col 0 opens slash autocomplete; '@' opens mention autocomplete; triple-esc is an interrupt counter (first esc arms 'again to interrupt', >=2 within 5s aborts the session); history up/down at buffer edges; paste auto-detects images/PDF/SVG/file paths and summarizes long text.
- Routing is a tiny createStore over a discriminated union (home | session | plugin) with navigate(reconcile(route)); App Switches on route.data.type. No router library. Editor/IDE integration (editor context), workspace sessions, frecency (file ranking), prompt history, and prompt stash are each isolated context providers — clean separation of cross-cutting concerns.
- Theming is strictly token-based (theme.background, theme.text, theme.textMuted, theme.primary, theme.border, theme.warning, theme.error, theme.accent, syntax styles) with a 30+ theme JSON set and light/dark mode lock — no hardcoded colors anywhere in the components read. This matches AGI's existing no-hardcoded-colors rule.
- Verified current vs official sst/opencode dev branch (GitHub API, 2026-06-01): architecture identical. Local snapshot is v1.14.30; dev shows minor drift — the keybinding module moved from `context/keybind.tsx` to a top-level `keymap.tsx`, and dev added `attention.ts` + `context/sync-v2.tsx`/`path-format.tsx`/`thinking.ts`. Core patterns (command registry, dialog stack, prompt parts, autocomplete) are stable across both.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- Adopt the unified command-registry pattern in Rust: define one `Command { id, title, keybind: Option<KeyChord>, slash: Option<Slash>, category, suggested, hidden, run: fn(&mut App) }` collection that simultaneously powers (a) the command palette, (b) global key dispatch, and (c) `/slash` autocomplete. Ratatui translation: a `Vec<Command>` (or registry struct) the event loop matches against on each KeyEvent, and the palette/slash filters render from the same Vec. Avoids the AGI pattern of separate keymap and palette tables drifting apart.
- Implement dialogs as an explicit modal stack with esc-pop and focus restoration. Ratatui has no focus engine, so model it as `Vec<Dialog>` in App state where esc pops the top entry and restores a saved `focus_target` enum (Prompt | Transcript | Sidebar). Render only the top dialog as a centered overlay (Clear + a sized Block) over a dimmed background. This is directly portable and matches what AGI's tui/approval_broker + transcript panes will need.
- Build one generic fuzzy-select widget (the DialogSelect analog) and reuse it for model/agent/theme/session/command pickers. In Rust use the `nucleo` or `fuzzy-matcher` crate for scoring, support category grouping with headers, a 'current' marker, type-to-filter input, and arrow/ctrl-p/ctrl-n/pageup/home-end navigation. Critical detail to copy: track an input-mode flag (Keyboard|Mouse) and ignore mouse-hover selection changes that fire while the list is re-filtering, otherwise the cursor jumps.
- Model the prompt as buffer + parallel parts, not a flat string. Keep `input: String` plus `Vec<Part>` where each Part {kind: Text|File|Agent|Paste, byte_range: Range<usize>, payload}. Render file/agent mentions and large pastes as short inline tokens, and expand them to full text/attachments only at submit. Re-derive byte ranges on every edit (OpenCode uses native extmarks; Ratatui has no equivalent, so recompute spans on input change). This unlocks @file mentions, agent handoff, and paste-as-attachment cleanly.
- Copy the input-mode affordances that make OpenCode feel fast: leading '!' for one-shot shell mode with a distinct border color; '/' at column 0 and '@' anywhere to open autocomplete; a triple-esc interrupt counter (arm on first esc, abort on the second within ~5s) shown in the footer; up/down history recall only when the cursor is at the buffer's top/bottom edge. These are pure state-machine behaviors with no framework dependency.
- Add paste intelligence: detect pasted file paths / image-PDF / SVG and convert them to attachment parts; summarize long text pastes (>=3 lines or >150 chars) into a '[Pasted ~N lines]' token that expands at submit. In Rust this is bracketed-paste handling in the terminal backend (crossterm) plus a mime sniff on path-like pastes. Keep it behind a toggle like OpenCode's paste_summary_enabled.
- Keep theming token-only and reactive to a theme switch, matching AGI's existing no-hardcoded-colors lock. Define a `Theme` struct (background, text, text_muted, primary, border, warning, error, accent, syntax) loaded from JSON, support light/dark + a mode lock, and never reference literal colors in widget code. OpenCode's 30+ theme JSON files are a good schema reference.
- Decompose cross-cutting state into focused modules the way OpenCode uses context providers — separate owners for keymap, theme, route, sync, history, frecency (file ranking for @-mention ordering), and stash. In Rust this is distinct structs/fields on App (no DI container needed). Frecency-ranked file completion in particular noticeably improves @-mention UX and is cheap to implement (recency+frequency score per path).
- Treat the local clone as v1.14.30 and re-verify against sst/opencode `dev` before copying fine details: the keybinding module is `context/keybind.tsx` locally but has moved to top-level `keymap.tsx` upstream, and dev adds attention/sync-v2/thinking modules. Pin to a known ref when extracting specifics.

**Conflicts (docs vs local reference)**

- No docs-vs-code contradiction found: the OpenTUI/SolidJS architecture is corroborated by both the local source imports (@opentui/solid, @opentui/core in app.tsx) and official docs (opentui.com states OpenTUI powers OpenCode). Where primary source code (the imports) is the strongest evidence, it wins, and the docs agree.
- Version drift (not a true conflict), verified via GitHub API on 2026-06-01: the local reference is v1.14.30 and exposes the keybinding logic as `tui/context/keybind.tsx`; the official `dev` branch has removed that file and added a top-level `tui/keymap.tsx` (plus `attention.ts`, `context/sync-v2.tsx`, `context/path-format.tsx`, `context/thinking.ts`). The live dev branch wins as the current source of truth; the local snapshot is accurate but slightly behind. Core patterns are unchanged across both.

## OpenCode Plugin SDK (@opencode-ai/plugin) — manifest, hooks, TUI/command extension, and discovery; requirements for AGI's /plugins + /marketplace panels

<a id="opencode-plugin"></a>

OpenCode ships a TypeScript plugin SDK, @opencode-ai/plugin (local ref v1.14.30; npm latest 1.15.13 as of 2026-06-01), with two entrypoint kinds exported from one default-exported module: a `server` plugin (runs in the engine, returns a `Hooks` object) and a `tui` plugin (runs in the OpenTUI/SolidJS TUI, receives a `TuiPluginApi`). Server hooks cover ~25 lifecycle points (chat.params/headers/message, tool.execute.before/after, tool.definition, permission.ask, command.execute.before, shell.env, auth, provider, plus experimental compaction/transform hooks) and custom `tool()` definitions. The TUI API lets plugins register commands, routes, slots (named host injection points like sidebar_content, session_prompt), dialogs, toasts, keybinds, and exposes a plugin-manager surface (list/activate/deactivate/add/install). Plugin "manifests" are ordinary npm package.json: discovery keys are `exports["./server"]`, `exports["./tui"]`, `main` (server fallback), `oc-themes` (theme-only), optional `engines.opencode` semver gate, and an exported `id` (required for file plugins). Plugins load from two sources — npm packages listed in the config `plugin` array, and auto-discovered local files in `{plugin,plugins}/*.{ts,js}` under `.opencode/` (project) and `~/.config/opencode/` (global) — with no native marketplace/registry: discovery is a PR-curated ecosystem web page plus awesome-opencode/opencode.cafe, and the only in-app install is the TUI panel's "install by npm package name" prompt. Note a verified post-reference API drift: v1.14.42 removed the `api.command.*` namespace (used by the v1.14.30 /plugins panel) in favor of `api.keymap.registerLayer({ commands, bindings })`.

**Key findings**

- ONE module, TWO entrypoint kinds. A plugin is a default-exported object that is EITHER {id, server} OR {id, tui}, never both (readV1Plugin throws if both present). `server` runs in the engine and returns a Hooks object; `tui` runs in the OpenTUI/SolidJS TUI and receives an imperative TuiPluginApi. For AGI (Rust/Ratatui), the server-hook model maps cleanly to a host-side trait; the TUI-plugin model is JS/Solid-component-injection and does NOT map to Ratatui without an embedded JS runtime + component bridge.
- Manifest = plain package.json, not a bespoke schema. Discovery keys: exports['./server'] and exports['./tui'] (each may carry inline {config} default options), `main` as a server-only fallback, `oc-themes` (array of relative theme paths => implies a tui target), `engines.opencode` (semver compatibility gate, enforced for npm plugins only), and package `name` (used as plugin id for npm). FILE plugins must export a non-empty string `id` or load is rejected. Entry resolution refuses paths outside the plugin directory (path-escape guard).
- Two load sources, four-stage load order. (1) npm packages in the config `plugin` array (string or [string, options] tuple), installed on demand via Bun into ~/.cache/opencode/node_modules/; (2) auto-discovered local files matching glob `{plugin,plugins}/*.{ts,js}` under .opencode/ (project) and ~/.config/opencode/ (global). Load order: global config > project config > global plugin dir > project plugin dir; deduped by package name (npm) or exact file URL, last-wins.
- Server Hooks surface (~25): event, config, tool (custom tool map), auth, provider, chat.message/params/headers, permission.ask, command.execute.before, tool.execute.before/after, tool.definition (mutate description/params sent to LLM), shell.env, plus experimental.\* (chat.messages.transform, chat.system.transform, session.compacting, compaction.autocontinue, text.complete). Hooks are mutate-output-in-place async fns. Custom tools use a tool() helper with a Zod arg schema and an execute(args, ctx) returning string|{output,metadata}; a plugin tool overrides a built-in of the same name.
- TUI extension API (TuiPluginApi) is rich and imperative: command.register(()=>TuiCommand[]) (title/value/category/keybind/slash/onSelect), route.register/navigate (reserved names home, session), slots.register + named host slots (app, home_prompt, session_prompt, sidebar_title/content/footer, etc.) for injecting Solid JSX, ui.Dialog/DialogAlert/DialogConfirm/DialogPrompt/DialogSelect + a dialog stack (replace/clear/setSize), ui.toast, keybind.create/match/print, theme (RGBA token map + install), kv store, reactive state (sessions/diffs/todos/lsp/mcp/permissions), event bus, and a plugins manager (list/activate/deactivate/add/install).
- The built-in /plugins panel is itself an internal TUI plugin (id internal:plugin-manager). UX to copy: a DialogSelect list sorted Internal-last, each row showing id + source path + an active/inactive/disabled status badge; space toggles activate/deactivate; shift+i opens an install prompt that takes an npm package name with Tab toggling local/global scope; on install it resolves+installs, JSONC-patches the right config file, then add()s to load in-session with success/warning toasts ('restart TUI to retry' on runtime-load failure). Responsive dialog sizing (medium/large/xlarge by terminal width).
- Install writes config, it does not maintain a separate enabled-state DB. install(spec,{global}) resolves the npm target then JSONC-patches the `plugin` array — into opencode.json for a server target and tui.json for a tui target (separate config files per kind), under .opencode/ (local, git-worktree-rooted) or ~/.config/opencode/ (global). A flock guards concurrent patches; existing duplicate specs are de-duped/replaced.
- Plugin lifecycle metadata is tracked in ~/.local/state .../plugin-meta.json (Global.Path.state): per-plugin fingerprint = target|mtime (file) or target|requested|version (npm), with first_time/last_time/time_changed/load_count and a state of first|updated|same. This drives 'changed since last run' detection and theme caching — useful prior art for an AGI plugin-state ledger.
- There is NO native plugin marketplace, registry, gallery, or in-app browse/install-by-search in OpenCode. 'marketplace' in the repo refers only to the VS Code extension marketplace (ide.mdx). Plugin discovery is entirely external: a PR-curated /docs/ecosystem page plus awesome-opencode and opencode.cafe. The only in-app install affordance is the TUI panel typing a literal npm package name. So AGI's /marketplace panel would be building net-new capability OpenCode lacks.
- VERIFIED version drift / conflict: the local reference is @opencode-ai/plugin v1.14.30; npm latest is 1.15.13 (2026-06-01). In v1.14.42 the entire api.command.\* TUI namespace (register/trigger/show) was removed with no deprecation, replaced by api.keymap.registerLayer({ commands, bindings }); the v1.14.30 /plugins panel code still calls api.command.register. The canonical repo is anomalyco/opencode (rename of sst/opencode, same Anomaly/SST team), so this is upstream truth, not a fork artifact.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- Adopt OpenCode's TWO-LANE model but pick lanes deliberately for a Rust/Ratatui CLI. Lane 1 (server/host hooks): implement as a stable Rust trait or a JSON-RPC/WASM host-plugin boundary mirroring OpenCode's Hooks (tool.execute.before/after, tool.definition, permission.ask, chat.params, shell.env, session lifecycle). This is the high-value, language-agnostic surface. Lane 2 (TUI component injection via Solid slots) does NOT port to Ratatui — do not promise arbitrary plugin-drawn TUI panels; instead expose a constrained, declarative extension surface (register slash-commands, list rows, status badges, toasts, key bindings) that the Rust TUI renders, rather than letting plugins render JSX.
- Use plain package.json as the manifest, exactly as OpenCode does — do not invent a bespoke manifest format. Read capability via exports['./server']/exports['./tui'] (or AGI-equivalent kind keys), main as fallback, an engines.agi (or engines.agi-cli) semver gate enforced for registry plugins, a required string `id` for local/file plugins, and an optional themes array. This buys ecosystem familiarity and lets shared tooling/lint reuse npm conventions.
- Implement /plugins as a manager panel modeled on OpenCode's plugins.tsx UX: a selectable list sorted built-in-last, each row = id + source/path + active/inactive/disabled badge; bind a toggle key (activate/deactivate) and an install key that opens a prompt with a local/global scope toggle; on install, patch the config file (JSONC-preserving) and hot-load in-session with success/warning toasts and a 'restart to retry' fallback. Reuse OpenCode's enabled-vs-active distinction (enabled = config opt-in, active = successfully loaded this session).
- Discover local plugins by glob ({plugin,plugins}/\*.{ext}) under a project .agi/ dir and a global ~/.config/agi/ (or ~/.agi/) dir, with a four-stage load order (global config > project config > global dir > project dir) and last-wins dedupe by package-name / file-path — this is OpenCode's exact, battle-tested precedence and avoids surprising override semantics. Keep server-target config and tui-target config in separate files if AGI splits engine vs TUI, as OpenCode does (opencode.json vs tui.json).
- Build /marketplace as NET-NEW capability OpenCode lacks, and treat it as the AGI differentiator: a searchable in-app gallery backed by a curated index (start with a static signed JSON manifest list, like awesome-opencode but machine-readable), with one-click install that funnels into the same install→config-patch→hot-load path as /plugins. Because OpenCode has only npm-name-typing, AGI can win on discovery UX. CRITICAL given AGI's local-first/trust-boundary rules: marketplace install of arbitrary npm code is a remote-code-execution surface — gate it behind explicit consent, a visible source/publisher label, signature/checksum verification, an offline/allowlist mode, and never auto-execute plugin code in a Local-trust session without user opt-in.
- Persist a plugin-state ledger like OpenCode's plugin-meta.json: per-plugin fingerprint (path+mtime for local, target+requested+resolved-version for registry), first/last seen, load_count, and a first|updated|same state. This powers 'plugin changed since last run' prompts, safe theme/asset caching, and an audit trail — all valuable for AGI's security posture.
- Pin to a current API contract, not the v1.14.30 snapshot. Before mirroring any TUI command-registration call, note that OpenCode moved command registration from api.command.register to api.keymap.registerLayer({ commands, bindings }) in v1.14.42. AGI should design ONE stable command/keybind registration primitive from the start (declarative layers of {command, key, desc}) so it never has to ship the kind of silent breaking change OpenCode did — and so /plugins and /marketplace both consume the same registration API.
- Honor an entry-path-escape guard and a compatibility gate as OpenCode does: refuse plugin entrypoints resolving outside the plugin directory, and enforce engines.<host> semver for registry/marketplace plugins (skip the gate for local dev file plugins). These two cheap checks prevent path-traversal loads and version-mismatch crashes, which matter more for a marketplace than for hand-placed local files.

**Conflicts (docs vs local reference)**

- TUI command registration API changed AFTER the local reference. Local ref (@opencode-ai/plugin v1.14.30, /Users/siddhartha/Desktop/reference/opencode/packages/plugin/src/tui.ts and feature-plugins/system/plugins.tsx) exposes and uses api.command.register/trigger/show. Current OpenCode (issue #26557, v1.14.42 via PR #26053; npm latest 1.15.13) REMOVED api.command.\* and replaced it with api.keymap.registerLayer({ commands, bindings }). WHICH WINS: the current online source/issue wins for describing present behavior — api.keymap.registerLayer is what ships today; the local v1.14.30 api.command.register is historical. Verified canonical via npm (latest 1.15.13 > 1.14.30) and repo identity (anomalyco/opencode is the rename of sst/opencode, same team), so this is upstream truth, not a fork. AGI should model the UX from plugins.tsx but NOT copy its api.command.register call as the current mechanism.
- Directory glob: docs say '.opencode/plugins/' (plural) while the config loader glob is '{plugin,plugins}/\*.{ts,js}' (singular OR plural accepted). No real contradiction — the loader is more permissive than the docs; code wins on exact behavior (both 'plugin/' and 'plugins/' dirs are auto-discovered). AGI should document one canonical dir name to users but can accept both.
- 'Marketplace' terminology: the repo's only 'marketplace' references (ide.mdx) mean the VS Code extension marketplace, NOT a plugin marketplace. Both local docs and the current ecosystem page agree there is no native plugin marketplace — no conflict, just a naming trap to avoid when scoping AGI's /marketplace.

## MCP elicitation + tools/resources/prompts spec — what AGI's Ratatui TUI must render for MCP requests and approvals (current GA revision 2025-11-25)

<a id="mcp-spec"></a>

The current GA ("Current") MCP protocol revision is 2025-11-25 (the versioning page names it explicitly; 2025-06-18 is the prior Final revision). Elicitation (server→client `elicitation/create`) is the only server-initiated user-input flow and is a CLIENT capability: clients MUST declare `elicitation` at initialize; in 2025-11-25 the capability gained sub-modes `{"form":{},"url":{}}` (empty object = form only). Form mode sends `message` + `requestedSchema` (flat object, primitive-only: string/number/integer/boolean/enum, plus `title`/`description`/`default`/`minLength`/`maxLength`/`pattern`/`format`/`minimum`/`maximum`, and—new in 2025-11-25—`oneOf`/`anyOf` titled enums and `type:array` multi-select enums) and returns a 3-action result (`accept` with `content`, `decline`, `cancel`). URL mode (new in 2025-11-25) sends `mode:"url"` + `url` + `elicitationId`; the client MUST show the full URL, MUST NOT pre-fetch or auto-open, MUST get explicit consent, opens in a non-inspectable system browser, returns `accept` with content omitted (consent only), then awaits `notifications/elicitation/complete`; servers may force this via `tools/call` error `-32042 URLElicitationRequiredError`. AGI's local CLI code (`apps/cli/src/mcp/elicitation.rs`, `elicitation_overlay.rs`, `tui_handler.rs`) already implements form-mode 3-action elicitation with a Ratatui overlay and async broker, but predates URL mode and the 2025-11-25 enum/default changes, and the desktop code models `elicitation` as a server (not client) capability. Tools are model-controlled with a human-in-the-loop approval SHOULD (show tool name+inputs, confirm sensitive ops, treat annotations as untrusted); resources are application-controlled (user picks via a picker); prompts are user-controlled (surfaced as slash commands).

**Key findings**

- Current GA revision is 2025-11-25 (versioning page = 'Current'); 2025-06-18 is the prior Final. AGI should negotiate `protocolVersion` and degrade gracefully: form-only behavior is valid for 2025-06-18 servers, but full 2025-11-25 support requires URL mode + the new enum/default forms.
- Elicitation is the ONLY server-initiated user-input primitive and it is a CLIENT capability. AGI (the client) MUST advertise `elicitation` at initialize. In 2025-11-25 the value is `{"form":{},"url":{}}`; an empty `{}` means form-only (back-compat). If a server sends a `mode` the client didn't declare, the client MUST return `-32602`.
- Form mode = `elicitation/create` {message, requestedSchema}. requestedSchema is a FLAT object of primitives only: string, number/integer, boolean, and enum. The TUI must render `title` (fallback to property name), `description` as helper text, pre-populate `default`, and validate `minLength`/`maxLength`/`pattern`/`format`(email|uri|date|date-time)/`minimum`/`maximum` before sending. 2025-11-25 adds titled enums via `oneOf`/`anyOf` ({const,title}) and multi-select via `type:array` with `minItems`/`maxItems` — the current AGI overlay handles neither.
- Three-action response model is the spine of the elicitation UI: `accept` (explicit submit; form mode returns `content` matching schema, URL mode omits content), `decline` (explicit no; content omitted), `cancel` (dismissed/Esc/closed; content omitted). AGI's overlay already maps [Accept]/[Decline]/[Cancel] + Esc=cancel correctly — this is the one piece that is spec-accurate today.
- URL mode (new 2025-11-25) is a distinct, security-critical render path the TUI lacks: server sends {mode:url, message, url, elicitationId}. Client MUST show the full URL with domain highlighted + Punycode/ambiguous-URI warning, MUST NOT pre-fetch/auto-open, MUST get explicit consent, then open in a system browser that the client/LLM cannot inspect; `accept` here means 'consented to open', not 'done'. Completion arrives via `notifications/elicitation/complete` (keyed on elicitationId) or never — so manual retry/cancel must remain available. `tools/call` may return `-32042 URLElicitationRequiredError` carrying the required URL elicitations to run first.
- Three different consent surfaces must stay distinct in the TUI: (a) tool-call approval (model-controlled; SHOULD show tool name+inputs, confirm sensitive ops, human-can-deny) — AGI's ApprovalBroker; (b) elicitation form/URL (server-requested user input, 3-action, may return content) — AGI's overlay; (c) resource picker (application-controlled selection) and prompt slash-commands (user-controlled). The ApprovalBroker's allow/deny decision cannot carry form `content`, so elicitation MUST NOT be funneled through it.
- For tools the spec is explicit about what to render: clients SHOULD show tool inputs before calling (anti-exfiltration) and confirm sensitive operations, and MUST treat tool `annotations` as untrusted unless from a trusted server. tools/call returns content[]/isError/structuredContent; input-validation failures should arrive as `isError:true` (not a protocol error) so the model can self-correct.
- Resources are application-driven (render a picker/tree/list the user selects from; support search/filter; optional subscribe + `notifications/resources/updated` and `notifications/resources/list_changed`). Prompts are user-controlled and should surface as slash commands (`prompts/list`→`prompts/get`), which aligns with a CLI/TUI command palette.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- FORM OVERLAY — bring it to 2025-11-25: extend `elicitation_overlay.rs` to (1) render `title` as the field label (fallback to property key) and `description` as inline help; (2) pre-populate `default` for every primitive; (3) add titled single-select enums from `oneOf`/`anyOf` ({const,title}) submitting the `const`; (4) add multi-select for `type:array` enum with `minItems`/`maxItems` (checkbox list, Space toggles); (5) client-side validate `minLength`/`maxLength`/`pattern`/`format`(email|uri|date|date-time)/`minimum`/`maximum` and block Accept with a visible per-field error, since clients SHOULD validate before sending.
- URL-MODE VIEW — add a new, separate overlay variant keyed on `mode:"url"`: show server name + `message` + the FULL `url` with the registrable domain highlighted (Ratatui palette accent, no hardcoded hex) and a warning row for Punycode/ambiguous hosts. Do NOT pre-fetch or auto-open. Two actions only: [Open in browser] (= consent → spawn the OS default browser via a non-inspectable launch, then return `accept` with content omitted) and [Decline]/[Cancel]. After consent, enter a 'waiting for {server}…' state.
- COMPLETION + ERROR PLUMBING: handle `notifications/elicitation/complete` by matching `elicitationId` to the waiting overlay and resuming; ignore unknown/already-completed IDs. Keep a manual 'Retry'/'Cancel' affordance in the waiting state because the notification is optional and may never arrive. In the tool-call path, detect `-32042 URLElicitationRequiredError`, surface its `data.elicitations[]` (each URL-mode) as URL overlays, and retry the original `tools/call` after they complete.
- CAPABILITY DECLARATION — fix the trust-boundary modeling: AGI is the MCP CLIENT, so advertise `elicitation` in ClientCapabilities at initialize with exactly the modes the TUI implements (`{"form":{}}` until URL mode ships, then `{"form":{},"url":{}}`). The desktop `ServerCapabilitiesV2.elicitation`/`ClientCapabilities` modeling has this backwards and must be corrected, or servers will (correctly) refuse to send elicitations.
- KEEP THE THREE-ACTION CONTRACT EXACTLY: Accept→`{action:accept, content:{…schema-shaped…}}` (omit content for URL mode); explicit reject→`{action:decline}`; Esc/dismiss/close/browser-fail→`{action:cancel}`. AGI's current overlay already does this — do not regress it when adding the new field types.
- ROUTE ELICITATION THROUGH THE OVERLAY, NOT THE BROKER: the `ApprovalRequestKind::McpElicitation` variant returns an `ApprovalDecision` (allow/deny) that cannot carry form `content`. Wire `elicitation/create` to `TuiElicitationHandler` + `elicitation_overlay` (which already collects content), and reserve `ApprovalBroker` for exec/file/patch/tool-call approvals. For tool-call approvals, render the tool name + arguments JSON before sending (spec: show inputs to prevent exfiltration) and present tool `annotations` as untrusted/server-supplied hints only.
- ALWAYS LABEL THE SERVER: every elicitation overlay (form and URL) MUST show which MCP server is asking — AGI's title bar already does 'MCP Request: {server}'. Extend the same labeling to tool-call approvals and the resource picker so the user always knows the originating server (a spec MUST for elicitation, SHOULD for tools).
- TASKS IS EXPERIMENTAL, NOT GA: the 2025-11-25 changelog marks the tasks utility 'experimental'; AGI's desktop `protocol.rs` comments/treat it as a settled 'spec 2025-11-25' primitive. Gate Tasks UI behind an experimental flag and prefer the `execution.taskSupport` per-tool negotiation surfaced in tools/list (`forbidden`|`optional`|`required`) rather than assuming task support.
- RESOURCES + PROMPTS UX: render resources as an application-controlled picker (tree/list with search; subscribe to `notifications/resources/updated`/`list_changed` to live-refresh) per the resource-picker model; surface prompts as slash commands in the TUI command palette (`prompts/list`→`prompts/get`, with required-argument prompts), matching the spec's user-controlled model and the existing AGI CLI command UX.

**Conflicts (docs vs local reference)**

- TRUST-BOUNDARY / CAPABILITY MISPLACEMENT (spec wins): The official spec declares `elicitation` as a CLIENT capability that the client MUST advertise at initialize (`{"elicitation":{"form":{},"url":{}}}`). In `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/core/mcp/protocol.rs`, `ClientCapabilities` models only `roots`+`sampling` and `ServerCapabilitiesV2.elicitation` is documented as 'server can request user input' — i.e. modeled as a server capability. Spec is authoritative: AGI (the client) must advertise elicitation, and the desktop type needs the capability moved client-side. (Servers do request elicitation, but the negotiated _capability flag_ lives on the client.)
- ELICITATION FORM SCHEMA LAGS THE GA SPEC (spec wins; it's implementation lag, not a doc error): `elicitation_overlay.rs` only parses flat string-enum/bool/text and ignores `title`, `default`, `oneOf`/`anyOf` titled enums, `type:array` multi-select, and the string/number constraint keywords — all of which 2025-11-25 requires clients to render/validate. The local code matches the 2025-06-18 form shape, not the current 2025-11-25 one. Resolution: treat the spec as authoritative and upgrade the overlay; current behavior is valid only when talking to 2025-06-18 servers.
- NO URL MODE IN THE CLI (spec wins): The 2025-11-25 spec makes URL mode + its strict client URL-handling rules (no prefetch / no auto-open / show full URL / consent / non-inspectable browser) first-class client obligations, and servers MUST use URL mode (not form) for credentials. AGI's `elicitation.rs`/overlay have no URL-mode path at all, so secret-collecting servers cannot be served compliantly today.
- APPROVAL-MODEL MISMATCH (both correct, but for different concepts — keep them separate): AGI's `ApprovalBroker` uses a 6-way `ApprovalDecision` (AllowOnce/AllowSession/AlwaysAllow/Deny/Cancel/Timeout) suited to tool/exec approvals, whereas elicitation requires the spec's 3-action accept/decline/cancel WITH a `content` payload on accept. The `McpElicitation` ApprovalRequestKind cannot satisfy an elicitation accept because `ApprovalDecision` carries no content. Not a doc-vs-doc conflict — it's a routing bug: elicitation must use the overlay/handler (which does carry content), the broker stays for tool approvals.
- TASKS: EXPERIMENTAL vs SETTLED (spec wins): `protocol.rs` comments label the tasks primitive as 'spec 2025-11-25' as though finalized; the official 2025-11-25 changelog explicitly marks tasks 'experimental'. AGI should not depend on it as stable; prefer the per-tool `execution.taskSupport` negotiation and feature-flag the Tasks UI.

## Ratatui 0.29 + Crossterm 0.28 terminal handling (bracketed paste, focus/resize, raw mode, alternate screen, title, capability detection, event-loop patterns) — for AGI's TuiEvent stream + FrameRequester

<a id="ratatui-crossterm"></a>

AGI's CLI pins crossterm 0.28.1 and ratatui 0.29.0 (Cargo.lock confirmed); current "latest" published is crossterm 0.29.0 and ratatui 0.30.0, so AGI is one minor behind on both. AGI's TUI uses a synchronous blocking event loop — `if event::poll(50ms)? { if let Event::Key(key) = event::read()? }` at tui_app.rs:450-451 and :2400-2401 — that matches only `Event::Key` and silently drops `Resize`, `FocusGained/FocusLost`, `Paste`, and `Mouse`. Terminal setup is hand-rolled (`enable_raw_mode` + `EnterAlternateScreen` only, no panic hook) when ratatui 0.29 already ships `ratatui::init()`/`restore()`/`DefaultTerminal` that do this plus install a panic-restoring hook. Although crossterm 0.28's `bracketed-paste` feature is on by default (so `Event::Paste` compiles), AGI never calls `EnableBracketedPaste`/`EnableFocusChange`/`EnableMouseCapture`, never queries `supports_keyboard_enhancement()`, and never executes `SetTitle` — the `terminal_title_setup.rs` widget only edits config and never writes the title to the terminal. Async EventStream is unavailable as-built because `crossterm = "0.28"` omits the non-default `event-stream` feature. AGI's `TuiAppEvent::RequestFrame` (app_event.rs:68, pane_view.rs:26) is its own render-on-demand abstraction; ratatui exposes no built-in FrameRequester primitive, so the canonical enabling pattern is a `tokio::select!` over `EventStream` + a frame-request signal + a frame-rate interval cap.

**Key findings**

- VERSIONS / RECENT CHANGES: AGI = crossterm 0.28.1 + ratatui 0.29.0 (Cargo.lock). Latest published = crossterm 0.29.0 and ratatui 0.30.0 — AGI is exactly one minor behind on each. ratatui 0.30 adds the new `ratatui::run(|terminal| ...)` closure helper (NOT in 0.29). The init()/restore()/try_init()/init_with_options()/DefaultTerminal helpers DO already exist in 0.29.0, so AGI can adopt them without upgrading.
- EVENT LOOP IS KEY-ONLY (the load-bearing finding): both loops are `if let Event::Key(key) = event::read()? { ... }` (tui_app.rs:450-451 and :2400-2401). Every non-key crossterm event — Resize, FocusGained/FocusLost, Paste, Mouse — is read and discarded. Enabling bracketed paste/focus/mouse is therefore a no-op until the match arm is widened to handle those Event variants.
- BRACKETED PASTE: compiled in but never activated. crossterm 0.28's `bracketed-paste` feature is ON by default (verified via docs.rs/crate/crossterm/0.28.1/features), so `Event::Paste(String)` is available in the type system. But AGI never executes `EnableBracketedPaste` (grep-verified absent), so the terminal never emits paste events, and the loop wouldn't match them anyway. To get true paste: `execute!(stdout, EnableBracketedPaste)` at setup + `DisableBracketedPaste` at teardown + an `Event::Paste(s)` match arm.
- FOCUS + RESIZE: AGI never calls `EnableFocusChange`, so no Focus events arrive (and the loop drops them regardless). Resize is partially handled implicitly: `terminal.draw()` re-queries backend size every frame, so AGI redraws at the correct size on the next 50ms tick — it is NOT visually broken, it just doesn't redraw immediately on resize. A dedicated `Event::Resize(w,h)` arm would give instant reflow.
- RAW MODE + ALTERNATE SCREEN: AGI's hand-rolled setup_terminal (tui_app.rs:467) does `enable_raw_mode()` + `EnterAlternateScreen` only — no panic hook. If the app panics mid-session the terminal is left in raw/alt-screen state. ratatui 0.29 `init()` does raw mode + alt screen AND installs a panic-restoring hook; `restore()` reverses it. Recommend replacing setup_terminal/restore_terminal with ratatui::init()/restore() (or try_init() for error propagation).
- TERMINAL TITLE: configured but never written. `widgets/terminal_title_setup.rs` is a checkbox overlay that builds a title string and saves config; it contains no crossterm import and never calls `SetTitle`. To actually set the title: `execute!(stdout, crossterm::terminal::SetTitle(title))`. This is a genuine end-to-end gap, not just a missing UI.
- CAPABILITY DETECTION: AGI does zero terminal capability detection. crossterm exposes `supports_keyboard_enhancement() -> io::Result<bool>` (kitty progressive-keyboard protocol) and `KeyboardEnhancementFlags` (DISAMBIGUATE_ESCAPE_CODES, REPORT_EVENT_TYPES, REPORT_ALTERNATE_KEYS, REPORT_ALL_KEYS_AS_ESCAPE_CODES) pushed via `PushKeyboardEnhancementFlags`/popped via `PopKeyboardEnhancementFlags`. Without DISAMBIGUATE_ESCAPE_CODES, key combos like Ctrl+Enter/Shift+Enter and key-release events are not reliably distinguishable on many terminals. Detect-then-push (guarded by supports_keyboard_enhancement) is the safe pattern.
- TUI EVENT STREAM MAPPING (deliverable): the input side of AGI's pipeline should be `crossterm::event::EventStream` (futures Stream<Item=Result<Event, io::Error>>, requires the `event-stream` feature — NOT currently enabled in AGI's `crossterm = "0.28"`), consumed via `StreamExt::next()` inside `tokio::select!`. Map crossterm `Event::{Key,Resize,FocusGained,FocusLost,Paste}` into AGI's existing `TuiAppEvent`. Today AGI uses synchronous poll/read, which cannot be multiplexed with the async approval_broker (Notify-based, approval_broker.rs) in a single select! — moving to EventStream unifies input, agent-turn futures, and approval waits.
- FRAMEREQUESTER (deliverable): ratatui exposes NO built-in render-on-demand / FrameRequester primitive — none surfaced in any official doc fetch. AGI's `TuiAppEvent::RequestFrame` + `TuiAppEventSender::request_frame()` (app_event.rs:96-98) and pane_view RequestFrame ARE its own abstraction and the right idea. The canonical wiring (per the ratatui async recipe) is a `tokio::select!` that multiplexes (a) EventStream, (b) a frame-request signal (mpsc/tokio Notify) so background tasks can request a redraw, and (c) a `frame_rate` interval that caps redraw frequency — coalescing many RequestFrame signals into at most one draw per frame interval. Use crossterm Begin/EndSynchronizedUpdate around draws to avoid tearing on fast terminals.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- Replace hand-rolled setup_terminal/restore_terminal (tui_app.rs:467-481) with ratatui::init()/ratatui::restore() (available in 0.29.0) to gain the panic-restoring hook AGI currently lacks; use try_init() if you want to propagate setup errors instead of unwinding.
- Widen the event match before adding any enable-commands: change `if let Event::Key(key)` to a full `match event::read()? { Event::Key(k) => ..., Event::Resize(w,h) => request redraw, Event::Paste(s) => insert text, Event::FocusGained/FocusLost => ..., Event::Mouse(_) => ... }`. Without this, EnableBracketedPaste/EnableFocusChange do nothing.
- Activate the features you intend to use at setup and reverse at teardown: `execute!(stdout, EnableBracketedPaste)` (and Disable on exit) for real paste; `EnableFocusChange` for focus dimming; only `EnableMouseCapture` if you want mouse (it disables terminal text selection, so make it opt-in).
- Wire the terminal title end-to-end: after the terminal_title_setup overlay saves config, call `execute!(stdout, crossterm::terminal::SetTitle(rendered_title))`. Right now the title is computed and stored but never emitted.
- Add capability detection: call `crossterm::terminal::supports_keyboard_enhancement()` after entering raw mode; if true, `PushKeyboardEnhancementFlags(KeyboardEnhancementFlags::DISAMBIGUATE_ESCAPE_CODES | REPORT_EVENT_TYPES)` to reliably read Ctrl/Shift+Enter and key-release, and Pop on exit. Guard so non-supporting terminals degrade gracefully.
- For the TuiEvent stream: enable the non-default crossterm feature (`crossterm = { version = "0.29", features = ["event-stream"] }`) and drive input via `EventStream` + `StreamExt::next()` inside the same `tokio::select!` that already awaits the approval_broker Notify and agent-turn futures — this removes the 50ms blocking poll and unifies the async surface.
- For FrameRequester: keep TuiAppEvent::RequestFrame as the signal, but consume it in a select! that also ticks a frame_rate interval (e.g. 30-60fps cap); draw only when a RequestFrame arrived since the last frame, coalescing bursts. Wrap terminal.draw() with Begin/EndSynchronizedUpdate to prevent tearing.
- Plan a routine minor bump to crossterm 0.29 + ratatui 0.30 (one minor each); ratatui 0.30 adds the `run()` closure helper that guarantees restore on early return — convenient but not required since 0.29 init()/restore() already suffice.
- Conflict to resolve in code: the two official ratatui pages differ — the async recipe hand-builds a custom Tui struct, the crate root recommends init()/restore(). For 0.29+ treat init()/restore() as canonical (it adds the panic hook); borrow only the recipe's tokio::select! event-multiplexing structure, not its manual enter()/exit().

**Conflicts (docs vs local reference)**

- No hard docs-vs-docs contradiction, but a recommendation divergence between two official ratatui pages: the async recipe (ratatui.rs/recipes/.../terminal-and-event-handler) hand-rolls a custom `Tui` struct with manual enter()/exit(), while the crate root (docs.rs/ratatui/0.29.0) recommends `ratatui::init()`/`restore()`. Resolution: for 0.29+ the init()/restore() helpers WIN as the terminal-lifecycle source of truth because they additionally install a panic-restoring hook the manual recipe omits; adopt only the recipe's tokio::select! EventStream-multiplexing pattern for the event loop. Verified against both URLs.
- Code-vs-capability tension (closest thing to a docs-say-X / code-does-Y in this repo): crossterm 0.28.1 docs say `bracketed-paste` is a DEFAULT feature so `Event::Paste` is compiled in — yet AGI's code never calls EnableBracketedPaste and its event loop only matches Event::Key, so paste is doubly inert at runtime. The docs are correct (the API exists); AGI's code under-uses it. Same shape for Resize/Focus/Mouse: present in the type system, dropped by AGI's match arm. This is a gap to close, not a doc error.
- My own mid-research assumption was wrong and is corrected here: I initially suspected `bracketed-paste` was non-default (like `event-stream`). docs.rs/crate/crossterm/0.28.1/features (accessed 2026-06-01) proves `bracketed-paste` IS default and `event-stream` is NOT. So Event::Paste availability is a no-op-without-enable issue, whereas EventStream is a genuinely-not-compiled issue for AGI (its Cargo.toml omits the feature).

## UX/architecture pain points in terminal AI coding CLIs (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode) — prioritized pitfalls for AGI's Rust/Ratatui CLI to avoid

<a id="public-feedback"></a>

Public UX pain in terminal AI coding CLIs collapses to three architectural roots, not many symptoms. ROOT 1 (rendering): full-screen-redraw + app-owned-viewport designs produce flicker, input lag that worsens as history grows, and lost native scrollback — the most-filed complaint class across Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini issues. Claude Code's response was a deliberate fork (official Fullscreen rendering doc): a classic renderer that keeps the conversation in the terminal's native scrollback (Cmd+f / tmux copy mode work) versus an opt-in alternate-screen renderer that eliminates flicker and keeps memory flat but must then re-implement scroll, search, mouse, and clipboard itself. ROOT 2 (input): missing/incorrect bracketed-paste handling causes the paste+Enter race (Claude #28137) and large-paste crashes/hangs (Gemini), because an embedded newline in pasted text fires submit before the buffer lands. ROOT 3 (approval): approval/permission overlays that cannot scroll their diff/detail, plus scroll-wheel input leaking into the composer (OpenCode #10923, #681). The local AGI reference (apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs) is code-verified to sit in the worst-of-both spot on Roots 1 and 2: setup_terminal() enters the alternate screen unconditionally, the event loop only matches Event::Key (no Event::Paste / no EnableBracketedPaste), the chat uses one app-owned scroll_offset with full terminal.draw() redraws, and render_overlay() renders approval detail with no scroll offset — so all three roots are currently live exposures.

**Key findings**

- Three roots, not many symptoms. Flicker + history-growth input lag + lost scrollback are ONE root: full-redraw + app-owned viewport. Paste failures are a SECOND root: no atomic bracketed-paste. Unscrollable/leaky approval prompts are a THIRD. Designing AGI around these three roots is far more actionable than chasing individual bug reports.
- Alt-screen is a FORK with documented costs, not a free win (code.claude.com/docs/en/fullscreen). Option A (classic/inline) keeps native scrollback, tmux copy mode, and OS-native copy for free. Option B (alt-screen) kills flicker and flattens memory but forces you to re-build in-app scrolling, search, mouse capture, and clipboard (OSC 52). AGI currently does B's screen takeover with A's tooling, none of B's required machinery, the worst position, reproducing Codex #18528.
- The paste race (Claude #28137) and Gemini's large-paste crash share one root: when paste is treated as keystrokes, an embedded newline triggers submit before the buffer is complete. Crossterm's EnableBracketedPaste plus an Event::Paste handler makes paste atomic and fixes both. AGI's loop matches only Event::Key, so it is currently exposed.
- Flicker is solved at the protocol layer, not by throttling: differential rendering plus synchronized output (DEC mode 2026) is what shipped to fix the multiplexer-jitter class (#9935-style reports), per the fullscreen doc. Ratatui already diffs cells; AGI additionally needs synchronized-output escapes and must avoid spamming scroll/redraw during streaming.
- Approval friction is a distinct, high-frequency complaint: prompts that cannot scroll their diff (OpenCode #10923) and scroll-wheel input bleeding into the composer (#681). AGI's render_overlay truncates long approval detail with no scroll, same gap, code-confirmed.
- Public-feedback signal note: the strong, specific UX evidence lives in GitHub issues across all four repos; HN/Reddit threads on these CLIs skew to cost/rate-limit/token complaints (explicitly out of scope), so they were not used as load-bearing sources.

**Recommendations for AGI**

- RENDERING - decide the fork explicitly and own it. Pick a lane: (A) inline/classic render that leaves the conversation in the terminal's native scrollback (recommended default - eliminates the entire Codex #18528 scrollback-loss complaint class for free and is closest to Ratatui's grain), OR (B) keep the alternate screen but then implement everything the Claude fullscreen doc lists: in-app scroll keybindings (PgUp/PgDn/Home/End + mouse wheel), an explicit dump-conversation-to-native-scrollback command for Cmd+f/tmux copy, mouse capture with OSC 52 + tmux-buffer clipboard fallback, and flat memory via render-only-visible. Do NOT ship the current state (unconditional EnterAlternateScreen in setup_terminal with a half-built scroll_offset and no scroll keys) - that is the worst-of-both.
- RENDERING - kill flicker at the protocol layer. Emit synchronized-output / DEC mode 2026 (BSU/ESU) around frame draws, rely on Ratatui's cell diffing rather than clear+full-repaint, and never re-emit unchanged scrollback. Throttle the streaming redraw cadence so token streaming does not generate thousands of scroll/draw events per second inside tmux (the #9935 jitter class).
- INPUT - make paste atomic. Call EnableBracketedPaste at terminal setup and add an Event::Paste(String) arm to BOTH event loops (currently only Event::Key is matched at tui_app.rs:451 and :2401). Insert pasted text as one unit; an embedded newline in a paste must NEVER trigger submit. This single change closes the Claude #28137 race and the Gemini large-paste hang at once. Also cap/stream very large pastes (Gemini crashed past ~2k chars) and show a [Pasted N lines] placeholder instead of rendering the whole blob.
- INPUT - keep paste/typing latency flat as history grows. The Claude paste-lag reports worsen with session length; ensure input handling and redraw cost are O(visible), not O(total transcript). With Option B this is automatic (render only visible); with Option A, keep the input widget's work independent of transcript size.
- APPROVAL - make approval overlays first-class scrollable views. Give render_overlay (tui_app.rs:1001) a scroll offset with j/k + PgUp/PgDn + mouse wheel so long diffs/command detail are fully reviewable (fixes the OpenCode #10923 gap AGI currently shares - detail is truncated to area.height today). Ensure scroll input inside an overlay is consumed by the overlay and never leaks into the composer (OpenCode #681). Surface the full command/file/diff before the decision so users never approve blind.
- NARROW-TERMINAL / RESIZE - reflow on resize. Recompute wrapping for the current viewport width on every resize so a window that was narrow does not keep narrow wrapping when widened (the Codex resize-reflow class, PR #18575). transcript_cell.rs already takes width into render_text - wire a resize event to re-wrap rather than reusing stale-width lines.
- Provide an escape hatch + clear status. Offer a flag/env to force the inline (native-scrollback) renderer for tmux/SSH/CI users, and always show which renderer is active. Claude shipped both modes plus toggles precisely because no single rendering choice satisfies every terminal - bake that optionality in from the start instead of retrofitting it after the same bug reports arrive.
